position.jp_title: Assistant Professor/ Associate/ Full Professor - Economics
position.jp_full_text:
Applications are invited at Amrut Mody School of Management (AMSOM), Ahmedabad University. We are interested in candidates in any field of Economics but particularly those working in areas of International Finance and Economics, Mathematical Economics, Industrial and Innovation, Health, Environment, Cultural and Heritage Economics, and Economics of New Technology.
Candidates at the Assistant Professor level must demonstrate the capability for carrying out high-quality independent research and should have completed, or be in the final stage of, their PhD. Associate Professors should have a track record of research and teaching. Professors are expected to provide academic leadership at the School / University. Suitable candidates may be considered for a joint appointment between AMSOM and the School of Arts and Sciences.
About Ahmedabad University Ahmedabad University is a private, non-profit, liberal education driven research university that has emerged as a centre for serious scholarship. Since its founding in 2009, the University has grown through global collaborative research, a contextual and flexible curriculum, interdisciplinary & project-based learning, and industry linkages, thus offering a unique learning environment and opportunities for academics.
Application Requirements: Letters of Reference Teaching Evaluations Research Papers Job Market Paper Cover Letter Curriculum Vitae (CV)
position.jp_keywords: Microeconomics Macroeconomics International Finance and Economics Mathematical Economics Industrial and Innovation Economics Health Economics Economics of New Technology Energy & Environment Economics Cultural and Heritage Economics

position.jp_section: Full-Time Nonacademic
position.jp_full_text:
​​​​​Economists at Amazon partner closely with business stakeholders, scientists, and engineers to solve problems across all Amazon business units. Embedded within a business unit or a central science team, you will build models on large-scale data systems to shape decisions that reach hundreds of millions of customers. Increasingly, economists work at the frontier of AI and Reinforcement Learning, combining causal and structural methods with machine learning to build and evaluate AI-driven systems. ​​​​ ​​​We value a broad range of applied econometrics skills: reduced-form and observational causal inference; structural estimation of preferences and strategic effects; forecasting, macroeconomics, and finance; all with strong foundations in statistical methods. Applied micro, empirical IO, mechanism design, health, labor, and public economics are all highly valued.
Basic Qualifications PhD in Economics, Finance, Quantitative Marketing, Operations Research, or a closely related field.
​​Preferred Qualifications We are hiring for all experience levels and fields but are focused on new 2027 PhDs. Strong track record in research, with a demonstrated ability to leverage AI creatively to improve its quality and innovation. Effective communication with both economist and non-economist audiences.​
Engagement Channels
Full-Time Employment (job market and post-PhD candidates): economist-careers@amazon.com
We hire on a recurring basis year-round.

position.jp_section: Full-Time Nonacademic
position.jp_full_text:
About Analysis Group:
Make an impact at Analysis Group, where we provide our clients with thoughtful, pragmatic solutions to their most challenging business and litigation problems—within a collaborative, inclusive culture that values curiosity, teamwork, and continuous learning. Analysis Group is one of the largest private economics consulting firms, with more than 1,500 professionals across 15 offices in North America, Europe, and Asia. Since 1981, we have provided expertise in economics, finance, health care analytics, and strategy to top law firms, Fortune Global 500 companies, and government agencies worldwide. Our internal experts, together with our network of affiliated experts from academia, industry, and government, offer our clients exceptional breadth and depth of expertise.
We offer cutting-edge analyses and analytical tools to address business challenges that require rigorous, evidence-based research. We collaborate with top professors from leading institutions to create a bridge between current academic thinking and real business issues. We assist premier law firms in many different litigation contexts, including antitrust, intellectual property and commercial damages, and with all aspects of litigation, including pretrial discovery, development of economic and financial models, preparation of testimony, and critique of opposing experts.
We advise corporate and government clients on a range of business issues that require expert interpretation of economic and financial data, including valuation of companies and assets, securities and financial instruments, tax and transfer pricing issues, cost-effectiveness analyses, market analyses, and evaluation of mergers and acquisitions. We also help organizations create strategies for growth by analyzing market dynamics and organizational capabilities, enhancing innovation in current products and services, and identifying new market opportunities.
We have received the Boston Bar Association’s President’s Award for the firm’s pro bono work on civil legal aid and homelessness, and the firm’s innovative approach to recruitment has been featured prominently in major outlets, including the Financial Times and Leaders magazine. We have also been recognized as a best place to work in several top national surveys, including Glassdoor’s Best Places to Work and Employees’ Choice awards (small and medium business category) and Vault’s Consulting 50, where we ranked 17th overall and as the top-ranked economic consulting firm.
About the Associate Position:
As an associate, you have the opportunity to work on complex business problems within an inclusive and collaborative environment. Associates can expect to work on multiple projects at a time across various practice areas and industries. Associates can expect to play a critical role in driving the research, analysis, and strategy of cases. Responsibilities may include:
Quantitative analyses and modeling: you will help lead the development of empirical models to address our clients’ needs using tools such as SAS, R, Stata, and Python. Qualitative research: you will contribute to and oversee the review of academic and industry research; you will evaluate client documents to develop support to address our clients’ needs. Preparation of reports/collaboration with experts: you will assist in the development of expert reports and other client deliverables; you will collaborate with internal and external experts to identify innovative, evidence-based solutions to our clients’ problems.
Team building and collaboration: you will collaborate with colleagues at all levels and across offices as part of your portfolio of casework, helping to foster a collaborative and inclusive team environment. Firm-building initiatives: you will contribute to firm life by participating in recruiting, mentoring, and inclusion initiatives; pro bono work; and business development and marketing activities (including marketing calls and pitch material development).
Analysis Group fosters a progressive and academically oriented work environment, with an emphasis on teamwork and collaboration across diverse areas of expertise. The ideal candidate will possess:
A Ph.D. in Economics, Finance, Accounting, or related discipline. Strong quantitative and research skills, including analytical and creative problem-solving abilities; familiarity with AI tools; the ability to apply targeted research to address client challenges; intellectual curiosity with a strong desire to continuously learn; and the ability to anticipate and respond effectively to opposing arguments. Clear and effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex ideas clearly and concisely. Demonstrated interpersonal skills and a collaborative mindset, with the ability to work independently and within a team setting. A strong academic track record, with demonstrated attention to detail, organizational skills, and a commitment to producing high-quality work.
We welcome applications from Ph.D. candidates at a range of career stages, including those with 2–4 years of relevant post-degree experience in academia, government, or consulting. We encourage these candidates to apply; role and responsibilities will be calibrated to each candidate’s experience.
Analysis Group embraces equal opportunity. We are committed to building teams that bring a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills, as we believe that a strong and inclusive workforce directly supports our goal of providing the highest-quality work. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or any other class protected under applicable federal, state, or local law, and we encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply.

jel_class.jc_description: Business Administration and Business Economics; Marketing; Accounting; Personnel Economics

position.jp_full_text:
The Department of Economics at Ashoka University invites applications for full-time positions at all ranks. The Department is among the leading economics departments in India, with a research-active faculty committed to excellence in both scholarship and teaching. The University is situated in Sonipat, Haryana, India.
Applications are welcome in all fields. Applicants must hold, or be close to completing, a PhD and must have teaching experience appropriate to the rank. For Assistant Professorships, candidates should demonstrate research potential through a strong doctoral dissertation and research papers. Applicants for Associate or Full Professorships must have a strong record of publications in peer-reviewed journals. The University provides an attractive salary along with research budgets.
Applicants must include a CV, sample research papers, a teaching statement, a research statement, and three reference letters. A cover letter may be included if any relevant additional information needs to be communicated.
Applicants should submit their application by November 30, 2026, for full consideration. Shortlisted candidates will be invited for virtual interviews.
The application should be submitted through Interfolio: https://apply.interfolio.com/193809
For further information, please write to eco.admin@ashoka.edu.in.

position.jp_full_text:
The Department of Business and Economics at Augsburg University invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor of Economics with an expected start date of August, 2027. Rank and salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.
Candidates must demonstrate a commitment to excellence in undergraduate teaching, a strong research background, and interest in Augsburg University’s mission and its diverse community of learners.
Main responsibilities include research, teaching undergraduate economics courses (including Money and Banking, as well as courses in the candidate’s area of expertise), and service. The teaching load is 3-3.
A Ph.D. in Economics or a closely related field is required.
Required Application Materials: Letter of interest, curriculum vitae, research statement, teaching portfolio (including experience, philosophy, and teaching evaluations where available), undergraduate and graduate transcript, and three references.
To receive full consideration, applications should be received online by November 1, 2026, but the search will remain open until filled. View the full job description and apply online: https:careers.smartrecruiters.com/AugsburgUniversity-MinneapolisMN/faculty.

position.jp_section: International: Full-Time Academic (Permanent, Tenure Track or Tenured)
position.jp_full_text:
The Research School of Economics at the Australian National University (ANU) is seeking expressions of interest from highly qualified candidates for the position of Lecturer or Senior Lecturer in Economics specialising in econometrics or empirical economic research, however any field of specialisation will be considered. Several tenure track positions are available. Tenure track appointments will be for an initial period of seven years, with the option of renewal or conversion to an ongoing position at the end of the initial employment agreement in accordance with the ANU Enterprise Agreement. The successful applicants will complement and extend existing research and teaching strengths within the ANU Research School of Economics and will be committed to high-quality teaching and excellence in research.
The ANU Research School of Economics is one of Australia’s premier academic institutions and provides an outstanding environment for economic research, teaching, and research training. The successful applicant will join a strong team of academics who publish in top international journals, hold external competitive grants, and receive recognitions for their sustained pursuit of educational and research excellence.
The ANU is one of the world’s great universities, ranking 29th in the 2027 QS World University Rankings. The ANU provides attractive benefits and excellent support to maintain a healthy work/life balance and offers generous remuneration benefits, including four weeks paid vacation per year, assistance with relocation expenses, and 17% employer contribution to superannuation. We also offer generous parental leave, a parental and aged care support program, dual career hire programs, staff and family tuition fee discounts, ANU school holiday programs, and childcare facilities on campus.
You'll find ANU in the heart of Canberra, Australia's capital city. The ANU campus is well renowned for its landscape setting and is an easy walk, bike ride, or drive from some of Australia's most significant political and cultural institutions including Australian Parliament House. Canberra’s beauty, accessibility and friendliness make it the perfect place to work.
Expressions of interest should be accompanied by at least three letters of recommendation. The initial interviews will be conducted online starting December 2026.
For more information, please contact Andy Martin, School Manager: schoolmanager.rse@anu.edu.au
position.jp_keywords: Econometrics Empirical Tenure track

The Business Department at Ave Maria University invites applications for a full-time, open-rank, non-tenured faculty position to start in the 2027-2028 academic year. Preference will be given to: Candidates with teaching, industry, and research experience. Candidates who have earned a doctoral degree in Finance or a closely related field. Candidates equipped to contribute to the University’s Catholic identity and mission.
Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States for full consideration.
The following documents must be submitted:
Cover Letter Curriculum Vitae, including a list of publications Graduate and Undergraduate University Transcripts (unofficial transcripts are acceptable initially, official transcripts to be furnished upon request) Teaching Philosophy as it Relates to the Apostolic Constitution Ex Corde Ecclesiae Research Statement: Research in progress and further interests Three Letters of Recommendation Optional supporting materials: Sample syllabi from courses taught, course evaluations
Review of applications will begin on November 1st, 2026 and will continue until the position is filled. Rank and salary will be commensurate with the candidate’s credentials.
Ave Maria University is a private Catholic university offering over 30 majors, including master’s and doctoral degrees. A Newman Guide School faithful to the Catholic Church’s Magisterium, our university provides one of the strongest classical liberal arts curricula in the country, as well as exceptional opportunities for specialized study in the sciences and humanities. The campus is located in sunny Southwest Florida, in the vibrant and growing town of Ave Maria, Florida.

position.jp_section: Full-Time Nonacademic
position.jp_full_text:
The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) invites applications for the position of Economist / Senior Economist / Principal Economist in its Monetary and Economic Department (MED). We are looking for talented candidates to join our global team.
As a forum for global central bank cooperation, the BIS plays a pivotal role in fostering collaboration among the world’s central banks. Economists in MED conduct cutting-edge research and provide in-depth analysis of key policy issues, serving as a hub for the central banking community. Their work reaches a global audience, including senior policymakers in central banks and supervisory authorities, academic researchers, policy experts, and financial market professionals.
By joining MED as an Economist / Senior Economist / Principal Economist, you will have the opportunity to:
Conduct innovative research on a wide range of topics relevant to central banks and regulators, Contribute to the preparation of policy notes for high-level meetings of central bank officials, Participate in policy committees and working groups, Provide expert advice to senior management within your area of expertise, Enjoy a unique, international environment that offers flexible, hybrid working arrangements, blending on-site collaboration with home office options.
Qualifications and requirements: a PhD in economics or finance, preferably in the areas headlined (Macroeconomics and Monetary Economics, International Finance, General Financial Markets, Financial Institutions and Services); a genuine interest in policy-oriented research; proven track record in identifying and addressing complex policy issues; and excellent writing and communication skills in English.
Who we are:
Internationalism is at the core of our identity, and the best representation of this is our workforce. With employees from over 66 countries and offices in nine locations, the BIS is a global organisation with a truly international workforce. By joining us, you will work in a unique, highly rewarding, and international work environment. We are committed to equal opportunities at the BIS and aim to build a workforce that reflects our global membership. We strive to attract the best talent and foster an inclusive environment. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, including those with a breadth of professional experience. You can discover more about our inclusive working environment here.
What the BIS offers:
We want your time at BIS to be a rewarding and career-enriching experience. We offer an agile and flexible working environment with hybrid working opportunities including home office and working from abroad days. To support our international applicants, we offer relocation support that extends to your dependent family members. In addition, thanks to our ongoing commitment to diversity and inclusion, we offer a competitive compensation and benefits package, including support for working families including childcare and education allowances (where applicable). Finally, we offer a genuinely unique international working environment, which will give you exposure to the global financial system and the opportunity to collaborate with passionate experts from all over the world.
Please apply with your CV, at least one recent research paper and three letters of reference via the link below by 8th November 2026. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to record a short introduction video and conduct a virtual interview. Candidates invited to the final round interview (which might take place on-site) will be asked to present a research paper in a 60-minute seminar, followed by interviews.
Please note that you should submit your application for this role only to one of these platforms: AEA's JOE Network.
position.jp_keywords: Macroeconomics Monetary Economics International Economics and Finance General Financial Markets Financial Institutions and Services

position.jp_section: Full-Time Nonacademic
position.jp_full_text:
Find out more about the Bank’s current research priorities, explore the broad range of staff research that our people have the intellectual freedom to pursue, and learn about the ways in which the Bank supports and collaborates with the external research community.
Important Information About this Position The position title used in this posting may differ from the official internal title of the position. Successful candidates will be appointed to either the Senior Economist or Senior Financial Sector Specialist Analyst position, as appropriate.
Application Process Your application must include the following: cover letter curriculum vitae research paper(s) or job market paper three letters of recommendation
Letters of recommendation should be submitted through Econjobmarket.
To apply, click on the link above or visit www.bankofcanada.ca/careers.
Application deadline Applications will continue to be accepted until all positions are filled. We recommend that candidates submit their applications by November 20th, 2026, as we will conduct virtual interviews as early as December 1st.
Your future responsibilities You will be expected to produce rigorous research and policy work to help the Bank’s senior management make better policy decisions for all Canadians. Your research will inform and help shape the Bank’s research agenda and support your department in providing sound policy advice. Subject to the needs and interests of the Bank and the employee, senior economists or senior analysts may move to other Bank departments to pursue research of relevance in new or needed areas. More specifically, you will be expected to:
Develop leading-edge research ideas, produce and disseminate high-quality research papers on Bank priorities Contribute to the core policy responsibilities of your department through model development initiatives, timely policy analysis and briefings to senior management Collaborate with researchers and policy staff within the Bank, and colleagues from other organizations on multi-disciplinary projects Build relationships with external parties-- e.g., government and international agencies, other central banks, financial market participants and organizations, and academia-- to share and receive feedback on research and analysis
Your education A recent (completed after January 2021) or forthcoming (completed in 2027) PhD in economics
Your knowledge and skills We will evaluate your application against the key requirements listed below and your education, which must be demonstrated in your cover letter, curriculum vitae, three letters of recommendation, and research paper(s) or job market paper.
If you are selected for an interview, you may be evaluated through two interviews and a presentation of your job market paper.
Key requirements Research skills: the ability to undertake in-depth and high-quality research projects that are publishable in peer-reviewed academic journals Alignment of fields of expertise with Bank priorities Writing skills: the ability to produce effective written documents in a style and form likely to appeal to and influence the intended audience Oral communication and presentation skills: the ability to make effective, well-structured presentations adapted to the intended audience, inside or outside the Bank, and the ability to communicate effectively with others by demonstrating active listening skills and conveying information clearly Teamwork and collaboration: the ability to work independently and collaboratively Innovation: the ability to create new insights, devise novel approaches and make innovative decisions through research Analytical and technical skills: strong problem-solving skills, including the ability to analyze complex economic and financial information using empirical and/or modelling skills No minimum post-PhD employment experience required; relevant doctoral research experience will be considered
Language requirement: English or French essential (verbal and written)
In exceptional circumstances, an equivalent combination of a PhD and research experience in an area of current particular relevance or interest to the Bank not listed above may be considered.
Research support, collaboration and development The Bank of Canada is committed to employee growth and career development and supports employees in reaching their full potential within their roles. As part of the career path in this position, it is possible to progress to a role with an expanded scope at a higher job grade, and a corresponding salary increase, if specific criteria are met. Travel for external presentations of ongoing research is centrally funded and managed by a committee comprised of Senior Researchers. Additional funding may be available for working with co-authors, invited discussions, or attending high-profile conferences. Support is provided by Research Assistants who help gather data, conduct statistical analysis, and prepare materials for presentations, and by a talented team of administrative, computer, data-scientist, editorial, design, and library professionals. Access to numerous data sources, including confidential and administrative data, and powerful computing capabilities, including the cluster. A variety of vehicles for external distribution of research and analytical work. These include personal web pages, Staff Working Paper series, Staff Discussion Paper series, the Staff Analytical Notes series, and Technical Reports. Many opportunities to interact and exchange ideas, provide feedback on ongoing research, and collaborate on research projects with economists from top economic departments and major institutions, with potential referees, and journal editors by offering: o a steady stream of research conferences, workshops, and visiting speaker seminars throughout the year including the Fellowship Program and the Visiting Scholar Program. o the opportunity to work alongside several Special Advisors whose role is to enhance the research efforts and policy advice by providing guidance on joint research projects (i.e., commenting on papers and policy documents).
What you can expect from us This is a great opportunity to join a leading organization and be part of a high-performing team. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to meet your needs at every stage of your life and career.
Salary The Bank offers a competitive total compensation package that is reviewed annually. The starting base salaries are based on qualifications and range annually between CAD $114,952.50 and CAD $156,778.00.
The salaries currently indicated are based on the 2026 salary scales. The Bank’s salary structure is reviewed regularly to ensure that the total compensation (salary and benefits) offered to employees continues to be competitive. In 2027, the salaries indicated above could be adjusted in accordance with the Bank’s annual salary review process, and this poster will be updated to reflect any changes.
Hiring bonus You may be eligible for a hiring bonus payable as a lump sum payment at the time of hire and up to two additional annual payments, for a total maximum of up to 30% of your base salary.
Performance pay The Bank offers an incentive for successfully meeting expectations at 7 to 10% of your base salary. The Bank offers additional performance pay (up to 10%) for those who exceed expectations. Additional Benefits Flexible and comprehensive benefits so you can choose the level of health, dental, disability, and life and/or accident insurance coverage that meets your needs Extra vacation days (up to five each year) that you can purchase to add to your vacation entitlement Indexed, defined-benefit pension plan The Bank offers flexible work arrangements, including teleworking, flexible work hours and work from away. For more information on key benefits, please visit www.bankofcanada.ca/careers/working-here.
Additional information Priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents Must be eligible for reliability status or secret clearance Work schedule: Full-time (37.5 hours per week) Relocation assistance may be provided if required Contact information: hrmobility@bank-banque-canada.ca North America: 1-800-303-1282 Outside North America: 613-782-8111 234 Wellington Street West, Ottawa, ON K1A 0G9 Number of available positions: Up to 8 Work address: 234 Wellington Street West, Ottawa, ON K1A 0G9 Position Type: Permanent/Full time
Let our team know if you need accommodation or support during the recruitment process due to a disability or other reason. We can provide support in multiple ways, from using this site and submitting your application, right through to the interview process. If you are the successful candidate, you can also discuss accommodation needs when you receive your offer. Contact accessiblecareers@bankofcanada.ca to discuss how.
We wish to thank all applicants for their interest and effort in applying for this position. Only candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.
position.jp_keywords: Senior Economist Senior Financial Sector Specialist Central Banking Monetary Policy Financial Stability Economic Research Policy Analysis Applied Economics Macroeconomics Financial Economics Research Economist Public Policy Data Analysis Modelling Empirical Research

position.jp_section: Other Nonacademic (Temporary, Part-Time, Non-Salaried, Consulting, Etc.)
position.jp_full_text:
The Bank of Finland's Research Unit invites applications for its Visiting Scholars Programme. We welcome applicants working in areas of interest to the Bank, particularly macroeconomics, monetary policy, and financial stability.
Timing and Duration Visits may take place anytime between March 2027 and February 2028, excluding July due to holiday season. Visits typically last one to two weeks. Visiting Scholars are expected to stay with the Research Unit for the full duration of their visit.
Applicants We invite scholars from academia, central banks, and other policy institutions. Applicants should hold a doctoral degree in Economics or Finance at the time of application and be active researchers. Preference will be given to applications that have the potential to develop into research collaboration with the Bank’s researchers.
Funding and accommodation We reimburse a single round-trip economy class ticket to Helsinki. We offer a remuneration intended to cover accommodation and food expenses. For visitors unable to accept Bank of Finland remuneration, these arrangements are negotiable. For example, we can cover accommodation costs directly.
Engagement with the Research Unit We encourage Visiting Scholars to actively participate in the Research Unit’s academic life, including attending research seminars and other research-related events, and presenting their work.
position.jp_keywords: macroeconomics monetary policy financial stability

position.jp_full_text:
Bates White specializes in providing advanced economic, financial, and econometric analysis to law firms, companies, and government agencies. We help clients tackle tough issues with confidence and pride ourselves on delivering top-notch expert testimony and consulting advice. But what makes us successful is our commitment to providing a positive and rewarding experience—for our employees, our clients, and the community.
Bates White, located in Washington, DC, is seeking PhD candidates and experienced PhDs to work closely with senior staff and partners on high-profile engagements. Responsibilities include economic research, empirical analysis, report and presentation preparation, and project management. The firm is looking for candidates who possess strong written and oral communication skills as well as the ability to think creatively, analyze complex data, develop clear, concise, and logical documents, and collaborate in teams.
We are seeking individuals interested in solving applied microeconomic problems. Expertise in industrial organization, labor, healthcare, econometrics, financial economics, applied microeconomics, or data science is helpful, but not required.
Our firm is recognized by leading academics and professionals as a premier place to work. Bates White has an innovative and entrepreneurial culture where bright minds from diverse backgrounds come together to solve difficult challenges facing legal, business, and government decision makers in the United States and around the world. In addition, the firm maintains strong relationships with key academics and industry experts.
We are deeply committed to providing a quality work experience and fostering and maintaining a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture. This is evidenced in the firm’s academic focus, career development programs, and employee engagement activities. As part of our quality work experience and supportive culture, here is what you can expect from us:
Competitive compensation—the salary for this position is $250,000/year. Economists are eligible for promotion review and bonus consideration every six months.
Comprehensive benefits package—includes low health care premiums, wellness benefits, generous paid time off, and more! To learn more about our benefits offerings, refer to: https://www.bateswhite.com/careers-life-benefits.html
Immigration support and sponsorship of visas and green cards.
A hybrid work environment with three coordinated in-office days/week with personal flexibility.
A team-based approach to client work where you’ll work side-by-side with peers, managers, and experts, making it easy to learn, network, and contribute to cases.
A transparent culture where your voice is heard, your input is sought, and your contributions are rewarded.
Investment in your career through intensive training programs, an assigned mentor and peer coach, and frequent feedback.
Networking opportunities through employee interest groups, our Women’s, International, and BWProud Networks, and our Engagement, Inclusion, and Diversity Council.
A fun and engaging culture including social events such as practice-area happy hours, team dinners, and firmwide celebrations.
Amenities including standing desks, a fitness center, a rooftop terrace, espresso, fresh fruit, breakfast and afternoon snacks, billiards, and ping pong.
Employee-driven community outreach featuring creative fundraising events (e.g., trivia, game shows, cooking competitions), volunteer opportunities, pro bono opportunities, and matching funds along with our pro bono program.
Application process:
For consideration, please submit a resume, cover letter, transcript, and job market paper. Please also send three letters of recommendation to aea2027@bateswhite.com. The application deadline is Sunday, November 8, 2026. If you are focusing your job search on economic consulting and would like to start the interview process early, please submit your application by Sunday, October 18, indicate your focus in your cover letter, and email our Talent Manager, Eileen Tharrington, at eileen.tharrington@bateswhite.com. For more information, refer to https://www.bateswhite.com/careers.html.
Bates White is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based upon race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, genetic information, protected veteran status, status as a qualified individual with a disability, or any other characteristic protected by law. If you are an individual with a disability and you need an accommodation or other assistance during the application process, please call our Human Resources department at (202) 408-6110 or email your request to careers@bateswhite.com. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply. Refer to the Know your Rights Poster for more information here: https://www.eeoc.gov/sites/default/files/2022-10/EEOC_KnowYourRights_screen_reader_10_20.pdf

position.jp_title: Assistant Professor of Sociology or Economics
position.jp_full_text:
The Baylor Interdisciplinary Core (BIC) seeks a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Sociology, Economics, or a related social science, beginning in August 2027.
The BIC is an integrated, team-taught core curriculum in the Honors College, emphasizing global and comparative perspectives on primary texts in historical context through small seminars and large lectures.
The preferred candidate will address questions of markets, morality, and economic systems through a primary-text curriculum. Relevant training includes economic sociology or anthropology, political economy, or the history/theory of economics. The candidate will pursue research that engages audiences beyond their home discipline and teach in two BIC sequences: World Cultures, Natural World, and/or Social World. Additional expectations include team teaching, mentoring undergraduates, and collegial service to the program, college, and university. Teaching and research expectations follow Baylor's Faculty Workload Policy.
Baylor, the oldest college in Texas, is an R1 institution in Waco serving 21,000 students and a ModernThink “Great Colleges to Work For” honoree. As a Christian university with historic Baptist roots, and as reflected in the Notice of Non-Discrimination, Baylor strives to be a place characterized by civility and respect.
Apply: https://apply.interfolio.com/192440
Candidates outside the U.S. without other nonimmigrant visa status will not be sponsored for an H-1B petition.
position.jp_keywords: Sociology Economics Moral Economics

position.jp_title: Endowed Bartlett Chair Professor/Associate Professor, (Free Enterprise)
position.jp_salary_range: Professor Rank Range: $160,000 - $260,000; Associate Professor Rank Range: $140,000 - $235,000
position.jp_full_text:
Bentley University invites applications for the Bartlett Chair of Free Enterprise, an endowed position at the Associate or Full Professor level, to begin in Fall 2027.
Funded by a generous gift from Bruce and Patricia Bartlett, the Bartlett Chair of Free Enterprise affirms Bentley's commitment to fostering free expression, intellectual pluralism, and the constructive exchange of ideas as central to a liberal education. Free Enterprise encompasses the institutions and conditions that enable individuals and organizations to pursue entrepreneurial ideas, enter and compete in markets, and create economic and societal value, while examining the legal, ethical, technological, and regulatory frameworks necessary to ensure fair competition and meaningful participation.
This position is part of a broader Bartlett initiative that also includes a companion Chair of Free Speech. The two chairs will work together to build programming, events, and curricular initiatives under the Bartlett banner that promote inquiry, debate, and engagement across disciplines.
The Bartlett Chair of Free Enterprise carries a 1-1 teaching load, providing substantial support for research, public engagement, and leadership of the Bartlett initiative. This support includes summer salary, a chair stipend, and a generous research and travel account.
Qualifications:
A Ph.D. in a related business, economics, technology, law or policy related field is required.
The successful candidate will demonstrate:
A distinguished record of research, teaching, and public engagement appropriate to appointment at the Associate or Full Professor level.
An active and high-quality research agenda that reflects a robust commitment to the principles of free enterprise.
Strength in interdisciplinary teaching and dialogue across fields.
We especially welcome candidates whose work engages some of the following potential areas of focus:
Entrepreneurship, new venture creation, and barriers to market entry.
Historical, ethical, and legal considerations in free enterprise and market/capitalist economies.
Competition, market concentration, and antitrust.
Regulation and its effects on innovation and business formation.
The role of digital technologies, such as A.I., in shaping market participation, innovation, competition, and entrepreneurial opportunity.
Candidates with experience in public-facing scholarship, civic dialogue, media engagement, or leading campus and community conversations are particularly encouraged to apply.
Responsibilities
Teaching:
Teach one course per semester, reflecting a 1-1 teaching load.
Offer undergraduate courses on free enterprise, free markets, and related topics.
Develop a Free Enterprise course within the Falcon Discovery Seminar (first-year program).
Foster rigorous, inclusive, and intellectually open classroom environments in which students can engage constructively with competing ideas and perspectives.
Scholarship:
Maintain an active and visible research agenda related to free enterprise, or closely connected areas of inquiry.
Publish in scholarly journals and public-facing venues.
Present research and ideas at national and international conferences, public forums, and professional gatherings.
Contribute to public conversations about free enterprise through writing, speaking, media engagement, or related activities.
Develop and sustain relationships with relevant scholarly, professional, and civic organizations (e.g., American Enterprise Institute, Heritage Foundation, or Cato Institute).
Campus Engagement and the Bartlett Initiative:
Collaborate closely with the Bartlett Chair of Free Speech on joint programming, including speaker series, public events, and curricular initiatives.
Help shape and advance a compelling long-term vision for the Bartlett initiative.
Lead campus conversations on the role of free enterprise and its place in society.
Working with the Dean of Arts & Sciences and the Dean of Business, the Bartlett Chairs will jointly shape a visible and intellectually vibrant set of initiatives that connect free speech and free enterprise as foundations of liberal education.
Bentley is committed to the teacher-scholar model, where teaching, scholarship, service, and community engagement are valued. Bentley values intellectual diversity alongside diversity of background and experience and seeks faculty who can contribute to a culture of open inquiry, free expression, mutual respect, and constructive engagement across differences in viewpoint.
Bentley University, located in suburban Boston, is an AACSB and NECHE accredited institution that enrolls approximately 5,200 students at the undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral levels. Bentley is ranked at or near the top in several categories by US News & World Report, including Best Regional Universities North and Most Innovative Schools, with Bloomberg ranking Bentley in the top 20 undergraduate business programs. Bentley’s high graduation and retention rates and top-ranked Pulsifer Career Center reflects a commitment to student success and inclusiveness. With a strong faculty of teacher-scholars, Bentley strives to be a “Force for Good” through the integration of business with the arts and sciences, and a strong emphasis on ethics and social responsibility. Providing a stimulating academic community for faculty, staff, and students, Bentley supports its faculty as they pursue cutting-edge research and bring their expertise and real world understanding into the classroom.
Application Deadline: For full consideration, applications should be submitted by November 1, 2026. Candidate reviews will continue until the position is filled.
Bentley University requires reference checks and may conduct other pre-employment screening.
Diversity Statement
Bentley University strives to create a campus community that welcomes the exchange of ideas and fosters a culture that values differences and views them as a strength in our community.
Bentley University is an Equal Opportunity Employer, building strength through diversity. The University is committed to building a community of talented students, faculty and staff who reflect the diversity of global business. We strongly encourage applications from persons from underrepresented groups, individuals with disabilities, covered veterans and those with diverse experiences and backgrounds.
position.jp_keywords: Free Enterprise Entrepreneurship Economic Freedom Competition and Antitrust Innovation and Regulation Markets and Capitalism

position.jp_section: Full-Time Nonacademic
position.jp_full_text:
Bring your research to the questions that shape markets, industries, and high-stakes legal outcomes. As a Managing Economist in BRG’s Economics, Disputes, and Investigations practice, you will work alongside leading economists, academics, industry specialists, and data professionals to apply economic theory, empirical research, and rigorous analysis to complex real-world matters.
BRG combines world-leading academic credentials with practical business expertise and a collaborative, entrepreneurial culture. Our economists contribute to significant litigation and consulting engagements, including matters involving antitrust and competition, intellectual property, securities and financial markets, and other complex economic disputes. With direct access to senior professionals and experts, you will have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of your work, expand your technical and leadership capabilities, and build a long-term career as an economic consultant.
BRG has been recognized by Forbes as one of America’s Best Management Consulting Firms and by Global Competition Review as a leading economics consultancy. Our continued growth creates outstanding opportunities for 2027 job market candidates who want to deepen their expertise, solve consequential problems, and develop in a firm that prioritizes intellectual rigor, collaboration, and career growth.
We are seeking Economists, Financial Economists, and Econometricians who are motivated to address complex applied economics questions. BRG supports the development of its PhD hires through hands-on engagement experience, structured training, and mentorship from senior staff and experts. Our economists work in highly collaborative environments across our Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles, and Washington, D.C. offices.
This position requires a highly motivated problem solver with strong analytical abilities, excellent organizational and writing skills, and a desire to collaborate as an integral member of our project teams. Ideal candidates will have prior experience or a strong interest in litigation or economic consulting.
Managing Economists execute and oversee engagement workstreams that may be quantitative or qualitative. Responsibilities include: - Designing economic, statistical, and financial analyses. - Developing models of financial data and markets. - Managing client relationships and developing and presenting client deliverables. - Managing and mentoring junior staff. - Conducting quality control and industry research and contributing to business development.
This position offers advancement opportunities within a rapidly growing expert services and consulting firm.
Qualifications - A PhD in economics from a reputable university, with a research focus in empirical industrial organization, applied economics, microeconomics, econometrics, finance, or labor economics. - Experience applying econometric modeling techniques. - Prior internship or work experience in antitrust, securities, financial economics, or capital markets is preferred. - A strong interest in economic, statistical, or financial analysis and research. - Experience using artificial intelligence tools to support research, data analysis, modeling, or other analytical workflows. - A strong record of technical expertise demonstrated through authored publications or research. - Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and analytical or relational database software, such as Stata, R, or Microsoft SQL, and a desire to expand those capabilities. - Excellent communication, critical thinking, analytical, and leadership skills.
This year, BRG is offering an early decision process for candidates who intend to focus their job search on private-sector economic consulting. To qualify, candidates must expect to complete their PhD by spring 2027 or earlier. The application deadline is October 18, 2026. To be considered, please submit a résumé, cover letter, job market paper, and two letters of recommendation using the link below. In addition, please email PhD_recruiting@thinkbrg.com to indicate your interest in the early decision process. Interviews will take place in November and December, and offers are expected to be made before the end of the year. Candidates who participate in the early decision process should be prepared to decide on any offer received before the American Economic Association (AEA) Annual Meeting in January.
For candidates following the standard AEA job market timeline, the application deadline is January 31, 2027. First-round interviews will be conducted virtually after the application deadline. Candidates who advance will be asked to present their job market paper and participate in additional interviews with BRG staff and experts at one of the listed offices.
BRG offers a market-leading compensation and benefits package. The base salary for Managing Economists is expected to range from $240,000 to $260,000, depending on qualifications, skills, and relevant experience. Employees may also be eligible for a signing bonus and annual performance bonuses, along with a clear path for career growth and advancement.
Salary Range: $240,000 to $260,000

position.jp_department: Economics, Watson School of International and Public Affairs
position.jp_full_text:
The Brown University Department of Economics and the Watson School of International and Public Affairs invite applications for a faculty position at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor in applied microeconomics (excluding development), with a particular focus on research that innovates methodologically while still speaking directly to policy-relevant issues in the world. The search is open to scholars applying for Associate and Full Professor positions, as well as scholars applying for an Assistant Professor position who have at least four years of experience since receiving their PhD. We seek candidates whose research makes creative and influential contributions to the scholarly literature in the field in a manner appropriate to their career stage. The successful candidate must also demonstrate the ability to engage with students, practitioners and an interdisciplinary range of scholars around the implications of their research for international and public affairs. Income and wealth inequality are topics of particular interest to this search, though they are not required and candidates without related work will not be at a disadvantage.
The position is expected to begin July 1, 2027. All candidates should submit: a cover letter describing research completed and planned, as well as how the candidate’s work would contribute to the research and teaching missions of our diverse and inclusive university community, a curriculum vitae, and, only for candidates applying for an Assistant Professor position, at least 3 recommenders via https://econjobmarket.org/positions/12562. To receive full consideration applications must be received by September 7, 2026. Applications will be accepted until the position is either filled or the search is closed.
Brown University provides equal opportunity and prohibits discrimination, harassment and retaliation based upon a person’s race, color, religion, sex, age, national or ethnic origin, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law, in the administration of its policies, programs, and activities. The University recognizes and rewards individuals on the basis of qualifications and performance. The University maintains certain affirmative action programs in compliance with applicable law.
position.jp_keywords: applied microeconomics methodology

position.jp_division: Thomas J. Watson Jr. School of International and Public Affairs
position.jp_full_text:
Brown University Watson School of International and Public Affairs and School of Public Health invite applications for a tenure track faculty position for a health economist at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor. The position is joint between the Department of Health Services, Policy, & Practice as the School of Public Health and the Watson School of International and Public Affairs. The search is open to scholars applying for Associate and Full Professor positions, as well as scholars applying for an Assistant Professor position who have at least four years of experience since receiving their PhD.
We seek candidates with a background in health economics whose research makes rigorous and policy-relevant contributions to the scholarly literature in a manner appropriate to their career stage. The successful candidate must also demonstrate the ability to engage with students, policymakers, and an interdisciplinary range of scholars around the implications of their research for public policy. We are particularly interested in scholars conducting innovative research in health policy or health economics. The successful candidate will join a vibrant interdisciplinary community of scholars working at the intersection of health policy, economics, public policy, and public affairs, with opportunities to collaborate across both schools.
position.jp_keywords: health economics health policy economics public policy public affairs

position.jp_full_text:
Assistant Professor of Economics | Bucknell University
B5 Current Heterodox Approaches
E6 Macroeconomics
Bucknell University is seeking a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Economics, beginning August 2027, specializing in current heterodox approaches. Candidates from any research field are welcome, with particular interest in emerging areas that expand the curriculum, including the economics of artificial intelligence and digital transformation, ecological economics, complexity economics, and macroeconomics.
Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in economics by the start of the appointment; candidates nearing completion will be considered. Candidates should demonstrate expertise in heterodox economics, excellence in undergraduate teaching, and strong scholarly potential.
The successful candidate will teach five courses annually, including intermediate macroeconomics and heterodox electives, advise students, and contribute to departmental, university, and professional service. Additional teaching may include introductory economics and interdisciplinary courses.
The department values pluralism, student-centered teaching, inclusive learning, collaboration, and interdisciplinary scholarship.
Application Materials: Submit one PDF with cover letter, CV, teaching portfolio (philosophy, evaluations, available syllabi, and inclusive teaching practices), research statement/sample, and official graduate transcripts.
Priority Deadline: Applications received by November 15, 2026, will receive full consideration.
Questions: Professor Geoff Schneider, Geoff.Schneider@bucknell.edu.
For full job ad and to apply, visit: https://apptrkr.com/9870086

position.jp_division: Division of the Humanities and Social Sciences
position.jp_full_text:
The Division of the Humanities and Social Sciences at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) invites applications for a tenure-track position in economics at the assistant professor level in the fields of experimental economics, behavioral economics, and economic history. Exceptionally well-qualified applicants in other fields and at more senior levels may also be considered.
Caltech is a world-renowned institute of science and engineering, committed to innovative research and teaching that prepares students to address fundamental social and technological challenges. We seek highly qualified candidates who are committed to a career in research and teaching. The initial appointment as an assistant professor is contingent upon completion of a PhD in a relevant field. The initial appointment for tenure-track positions is normally four years. Reappointment beyond the initial term is contingent upon successful review conducted prior to the commencement of the fourth year.
Interested candidates should apply electronically at https://applications.caltech.edu/jobs/economics. Applications should include the following: (1) cover letter, (2) current CV, (3) research statement describing research highlights and future plans, (4) an education statement that addresses the applicant's thoughts on classroom and laboratory instruction, mentorship of students and postdoctoral scholars, and ways to foster an inclusive environment for the development of scholars who come to Caltech with many different perspectives and experiences, (5) three letters of recommendation and (6) a sample of original written work.
Candidates unable to apply electronically may send these application materials to: Chair, Assistant Professor of Economics Search, California Institute of Technology, HSS 228-77, Pasadena, CA 91125.
The deadline for applications is November 1, 2026.
Salaries for professorial faculty at Caltech fall in the range of $125,000 to $400,000.
Caltech is an equal opportunity employer and, as a federal contractor, takes affirmative action to employ qualified individuals with disabilities and protected veterans. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.
Caltech is a VEVRAA Federal Contractor.
To read more about Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) go to “Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal” Poster | U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission.

Call for Applications: PERMIT Lab Postdoctoral Scholar Research Associate
The Policy and Environmental Research on Markets, Integration, and Trade (PERMIT) Lab at Caltech seeks a postdoctoral scholar research associate (postdoc) to start in spring or summer of 2027. The Postdoc appointment will run for two years, unless a shorter term is mutually agreeable.
This position is designed for an entrepreneurial, PhD-level researcher with a strong interest in academic work or environmental policy work. The postdoctoral scholar will report primarily to faculty member Prakash Mishra but will additionally be part of a vibrant community of other postdocs, faculty members, and research staff focused on environmental economics from a variety of backgrounds. Opportunities for collaboration include ongoing research on the design of conservation easement programs and the impact of trade policy on environmental degradation and development in Mexico and Chile. The postdoc is expected to dedicate significant time to developing their own research agenda.
The ideal candidate has a research agenda in environmental economics with some background in remote sensing data. Candidates may use this postdoctoral fellowship as a stepping stone to a job in hand or as a chance to develop a broader research agenda before going on the market.
Requirements: Submit a CV and job market paper to prakashm@caltech.edu. Arrange for three letters of recommendation to be submitted to prakashm@caltech.edu.
Questions about the application process can be directed to the same.
The application deadline is rolling, with a first review of applications targeted for November 20, 2026.
Hiring Salary: $75,268
The appointment will include a discretionary fund of $5000 for conference travel.
As one of the largest employers in Pasadena, CA, Caltech is committed to providing comprehensive benefits to eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Our benefits package includes competitive compensation, health, dental, and vision insurance, retirement savings plans, generous paid time off (vacation, holidays, sick time, parental leave, bereavement, etc.), tuition reimbursement, and more. Learn more about our benefits and staff perks.
We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.
Caltech is a VEVRAA Federal Contractor.

position.jp_title: Tenure Track Assistant Professor of Economics
position.jp_full_text:
The Department of Economics at California State University, Fullerton (CSUF) invites applications for two tenure-track assistant professor positions in Economics with a focus on empirical research. We are particularly interested in candidates conducting research using machine learning methods.
Successful candidates will be expected to develop graduate and undergraduate courses in data analytics with economic applications and will play an important role in advancing the analytical focus of our STEM-certified MA program. They will conduct research in their field(s) of specialization, teach graduate and undergraduate courses in machine learning, as well as core graduate and undergraduate courses in their economic areas of specialization, provide service to the university, and participate in our community.
Applications received by November 15 are guaranteed full consideration. Located in a vibrant community just south of Los Angeles, the Economics Department at CSUF is part of the College of Business and Economics, the largest accredited business school on the West Coast. CSUF has a strong institutional commitment to fostering the diversity of its faculty, staff, and student body and is an Equal Opportunity and affirmative action employer. We actively encourage applications from scholars from a wide variety of backgrounds.
First-round interviews will be conducted virtually in early January 2027.
Please see the external application link below for the official position announcement and application submission link, along with instructions for how to deal with reference letters
Please direct all questions about the position to: Pedro Amaral, Department Search Committee Chair, at pamaral@fullerton.edu.
Application deadline: 11/15/2026
Qualifications: A completed Ph.D. degree in Economics at the start of the appointment (Fall 2027); Demonstrated research potential as evidenced by research record and ongoing research in their areas of specialty with a focus on data analytics; Demonstrated interest in teaching a diverse student population.
position.jp_keywords: Machine Learning Data Analytics Applied Microeconomics Applied Econometrics

position.jp_section: Full-Time Nonacademic
position.jp_full_text:
As a Quantitative Modeler at Capital One, you’ll be part of a team that’s leading the next wave of disruption at a whole new scale, using the latest in cloud computing and machine learning technologies and operating across billions of customer records to unlock the big opportunities that help everyday people save money, time and agony in their financial lives.
This position is part of Capital One’s Credit Risk Management Modeling team. In this team, we use multiple cloud-based open-sourced technologies to develop econometric and machine learning models and analytics to predict and generate insight into Capital One’s risk and capital needs. We blend cutting-edge quantitative methods with deep understanding of our business, data, and regulatory environment to build predictive models for credit and operational losses, volumes and outstanding balances in support of loss forecasting, CECL/allowance, stress testing, and capital allocation for Capital One. Our models and analyses inform earnings call prep, vertical resilience and downturn preparedness initiatives.
In this position, you’ll be part of a team tasked with ushering in the next wave of disruption to predictive modeling - using technology to build & deploy models and solutions leveraging new data sources to provide powerful new insights about our portfolio resilience and opportunities.
Responsibilities and Skills: Partner with the various lines of business to enhance modeling and analytical framework. Work across Capital One entities to create novel analytical solutions to the challenging business problems. Identify opportunities to apply quantitative methods and automation solutions to improve business performance and process efficiencies. Collaborate in a cross-disciplinary team to build cloud-based solutions grounded in data. Identify opportunities to apply quantitative methods or machine learning to improve business performance. Apply deep expertise in econometric, statistical and machine learning methods to generate critical insights and decision frameworks for our business and customers. Providing technical guidance to business leadership. Communicate technical subject matter clearly and concisely to individuals from various backgrounds.
Expertise in quantitative analysis is central to our success in all markets. Our modelers thrive in a culture of mutual respect, excellence and innovation.
Successful candidates would possess: Strong understanding of quantitative analysis methods in relation to financial institutions. Demonstrated track-record in machine learning and/or econometric analysis. Experience utilizing model estimation tools. Ability to clearly communicate modeling results to a wide range of audiences. Drive to develop and maintain high quality and transparent model documentation. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Strong presentation skills. Ability to fully own the model development process: from conceptualization through data exploration, model selection, validation, deployment, business user training, and monitoring.
Basic Qualifications: Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining one of the following with an exception that the required degree will be obtained on or before the scheduled start date: A Master’s degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) or an MBA with a quantitative concentration plus 3 years of experience in quantitative analytics A PhD in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field)
At least 3 years of experience in each of the following skills through education or experience:
Statistical or econometric modeling Linear and logistic regression Programming in R, Python or SQL Presenting statistical concepts and research results to non-statistical audience
At least 3 years of experience in at least 3 of the following skills:
Survival analysis modeling Time-series analysis Panel data (longitudinal data or cross-sectional time-series data) analysis Cross-sectional data analysis Machine learning Analysis and management of large datasets (>1M records)
Preferred Qualifications:
4 years of experience with Python, R or other statistical analyst software 4 years of experience manipulating and analyzing large data sets
Capital One will consider sponsoring a new qualified applicant for employment authorization for this position.

position.jp_section: Full-Time Nonacademic
position.jp_full_text:
The Market Shaping Accelerator (MSA) housed at the Center for Global Development is hiring a Fellow or Senior Fellow to lead research and policy work on market shaping, pull incentives, and innovation.
MSA designs advance market commitments, prizes, milestone payments, and other mechanisms that align private incentives with social value and accelerate innovation in global health, pandemic preparedness, climate, AI safety, and drug repurposing.
The successful candidate will lead a research agenda combining economic theory, industrial organization, market design, quantitative analysis, and policy design. Responsibilities include producing policy-relevant research, engaging policymakers and funders, mobilizing funding, representing MSA externally, and mentoring staff.
Applicants should hold, or expect to complete before starting, a PhD in economics and should also have experience with (or demonstrated interest in) translating research into policy. The position is based in CGD’s Washington, DC office, with at least three in-office days per week. Employees must reside in DC, Maryland, or Virginia. Visa sponsorship is available.
Apply in the external link below with (1) a cover letter, (2) a writing sample and (3) a CV. Candidates will be reviewed in two cycles after Nov 1, 2026 and February 1, 2027, with virtual interviews following each.
position.jp_keywords: Innovation Economics Market Shaping Advanced Market Commitments Market Design Industrial Organization Global Health Climate Policy Pull Incentives

position.jp_full_text: The Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (CBRT) seeks highly qualified candidates for Economist positions with strong potential to contribute substantially to research and policy analysis. Successful candidates will conduct both independent and policy-directed research on central banking issues and will contribute to the policy-making process. Strong oral and written communication skills are required, along with excellent analytical and quantitative skills. Candidates should be able to present complex economic analysis clearly to diverse audiences. Economists at the CBRT work closely with policymakers and regularly present their analysis as part of the Bank’s decision-making process. At the same time, the CBRT offers a stimulating and collaborative research environment, with generous support for research activities and conference travel, as well as access to a rich and continuously expanding range of economic and financial data. The Bank regularly hosts workshops and conferences that bring together researchers and policymakers from leading central banks, international organizations, and universities. Applicants must be Turkish citizens and meet the eligibility requirements in the CBRT’s employment regulations, except the age requirement. Candidates are expected to have completed, or to complete, a doctoral degree by the end of 2027. The CBRT offers a competitive compensation package and attractive benefits.

position.jp_full_text:
Centre College invites applications for a tenure-track position as Assistant Professor of Economics & Business, with a specialization in Macroeconomics, beginning in August 2027. We welcome applicants with research and teaching interests in macroeconomics, including macroeconomic aspects of public finance and open economy macroeconomics. Candidates must have a Ph.D. in Economics by the time of appointment. We encourage applications from candidates who are committed to undergraduate education and will utilize a variety of pedagogical practices. As noted in the Statement on Community, Centre strives to create an environment where differences are celebrated rather than discouraged.
The Economics & Business Program offers two degrees: 1) Business and 2) Economics & Finance. The teaching responsibilities include core and elective courses in the successful candidate’s specialty. The teaching load is six courses per academic year. The Program’s faculty is a highly collegial, dedicated, and accomplished group of teacher-scholars looking for a colleague who will contribute meaningfully to our continued growth and excellence.
Centre College is a highly selective college of 1,350 students with small classes and high standards, has one of the nation’s premier study abroad programs, and is ranked among the top National Liberal Arts Colleges by U.S. News & World Report. The faculty are dedicated to excellent teaching and student mentorship, shared governance, interdisciplinary collaboration, scholarly achievement, and service to the college and broader society. We support faculty from all backgrounds, offering early-career mentoring and ongoing professional development. Centre graduates enjoy extraordinary success, including study at top graduate and professional schools, prestigious fellowships, and rewarding jobs. Centre College is located in Danville, Kentucky, a town of 18,000 recognized for its high quality of life, friendly people, beautiful landscapes, and easy access to Lexington, KY; Louisville, KY; and Cincinnati, OH. For more information, visit www.centre.edu.
To apply, please submit the following at https://www.centre.edu/about/employment-centre . A complete application will include (1) letter describing your interest in and qualifications, (2) curriculum vitae, (3) a statement of teaching philosophy, (4) specific evidence of teaching experience and effectiveness, (5) three confidential letters of reference from individuals able to share insight into your expertise and future potential, (6) job-market paper, and (7) unofficial transcripts. For full consideration, submit your complete application by 11/20/26. Candidates with questions about access or accommodations for any part of the application process should contact Dr. John Perry at john.perry@centre.edu (Search Chair).
position.jp_keywords: Macroeconomics

position.jp_division: Institute for the Study of Religion, Economics and Society (IRES)
position.jp_full_text:
Postdoctoral Fellowship in the Economics of Religion
The Institute for the Study of Religion, Economics, and Society (IRES) at Chapman University invites applications for a Postdoctoral Fellowship in the Economics of Religion. The fellowship will begin in Fall 2027 and may be renewed for up to two years, contingent upon satisfactory performance and continued funding.
Founded in 2009 by Dr. Laurence R. Iannaccone, IRES is dedicated to advancing interdisciplinary scholarship on the relationships among religion, economics, and society. The institute brings together economists, sociologists, and other social scientists to investigate religious behavior, institutions, and their broader social and economic impacts. IRES supports this mission through a wide range of activities, including scholarly publications, research seminars, conferences, training workshops, academic courses, public lectures, and online resources.
IRES serves as the home of the Association for the Study of Religion, Economics, and Culture (ASREC) and is a partner of the Association of Religion Data Archives (ARDA). Through these affiliations, the institute has become a central hub within a growing international network of scholars and students engaged in the scientific study of religion.
position.jp_keywords: Economics of Religion

position.jp_title: Faculty Positions (Open Rank) in Economics at CEIBS
position.jp_full_text:
Faculty Positions (Open Rank) in Economics at CEIBS
The Department of Economics and Decision Sciences invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position (open-rank) in empirical industrial organization. We will also consider strong candidates from other fields. The school's working language is English, and faculty may choose to be based at any of CEIBS’ Chinese mainland campuses in Shanghai, Beijing, or Shenzhen.
Applicants must hold a PhD in economics or a relevant field from a highly regarded doctoral programme, with all degree requirements completed by the time of appointment. Candidates should demonstrate strong potential for publishing in leading academic journals and a clear commitment to teaching excellence. The successful applicant will be expected to pursue a rigorous and sustained research agenda, contribute actively to the intellectual community of the school, and teach courses at the MBA and executive level.
CEIBS offers one of the most competitive faculty compensation packages globally, commensurate with qualifications and experience. In addition to an internationally attractive base salary, the school provides a comprehensive range of benefits, including a generous housing allowance, education support for children attending international schools, premium family medical insurance, and a private pension plan. The school also offers generous research funding and reduced teaching loads in recognition of high-quality scholarly publications, thereby supporting faculty in achieving research excellence.
To apply, please submit a cover letter, a curriculum vitae, a sample research paper, evidence of effective teaching (if available), and three reference letters (for applicants for Assistant Professorship) via JOE Application. Applications received by December 1, 2026 will be given full consideration. Inquiries regarding the positions may be directed to Ms. Daisy Li at ldaisy@ceibs.edu. All applications will be treated confidentially and will be reviewed until the positions are filled.
About CEIBS Founded in 1994 as a non-profit joint venture between the Chinese Government and the European Union, CEIBS is widely regarded as one of the leading business schools in Asia. The school offers a full range of programmes, including the MBA – ranked No. 1 in Asia by the Financial Times since 2017, the Finance MBA, Part-time MBA, Global MiM (Switzerland), EMBA, Global EMBA – ranked among the global top two by the Financial Times since 2020, Hospitality EMBA, DBA (Switzerland), PhD, and a broad portfolio of Executive Education programmes. These programmes aim to cultivate responsible leaders with “China Depth, Global Breadth” and have fostered a global alumni network of over 35,000 graduates who actively contribute to economic and social development. CEIBS operates campuses in Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen, Zurich, and Accra.
CEIBS is accredited by both EQUIS and AACSB. Its faculty are internationally recognised for combining China Depth with Global Breadth in their research and teaching. The school’s research excellence is reflected in its strong performance in global scholarly rankings. In January 2026, eighteen CEIBS faculty members were included in Elsevier’s Highly Cited Chinese Researchers (2025) list – the highest number among all business schools in China. In September 2025, seven CEIBS professors were listed among the World’s Top 2% Scientists (2025). These achievements underscore the school’s growing impact on global management scholarship and its continued commitment to academic excellence.
