position.jp_full_text:
Description The Kenneth C. Griffin Department of Economics at the University of Chicago invites applications for a full-time Research Associate for a three-year term starting in the 2026-2027 academic year.
About the TMW Center Co-directed by Dana Suskind (Biological Sciences Division), and John List (Economics), the TMW Center for Early Learning + Public Health aspires to create a population-level shift in the knowledge and behavior of parents and caregivers to optimize the foundational brain development in children, birth to five years of age, particularly those born into poverty. The TMW Center has conducted 12 randomized controlled, quasi-experimental, and implementation trials to date and plans to continue its active randomized controlled and implementation trials, including ongoing data collection and analysis in the coming years. As part of these research projects, the Center is continuing to adapt and validate two state-of-the-art tools: (1) the SPEAK - a computer-adaptive tool designed to assess caretaker expectations and knowledge of early childhood cognitive and language development, and (2) the Luet – a wearable device paired with an app that uses machine learning to measure early child development through language and physical movement.
Job Summary: The Research Associate will work, in partnership with Co-Director Suskind and Senior Research Associate Pernaudet, to design and execute TMW Center research projects. Core responsibilities include conducting rigorous quantitative analyses, writing and publishing findings, presenting research, and leading grant applications in collaboration with Professors List and Suskind. The position entails collaboration on new and ongoing research projects, with a highly interdisciplinary team of economists, psychologists, engineers, app developers, and more. A primary focus of the work is applying economic models and machine learning techniques to empirical analysis of data generated from TMW Center’s research projects, including via Luet and the SPEAK.
The position will also allow the Research Associate to be part of the vibrant research environment of the TMW Center for Early Learning + Public Health and the Kenneth C. Griffin Department of Economics at The University of Chicago. This position will report to the TMW Center Co-Directors, Dana Suskind and John List, with additional reporting to the Center COO for matters outside of research. This position will require a commitment of at least 3 years.
This position is benefits-eligible. The University of Chicago offers a wide range of benefits programs and resources for eligible employees, including health, retirement, and paid time off. Information about the benefit offerings can be found in the Benefits Guidebook.
Responsibilities will include, but are not limited to: In collaboration with the Co-Director, develop research designs for TMW Center projects, including formulating testable research questions, selecting appropriate measurements, and ensuring clean identification of outcomes. At the direction of the Co-Director, write, submit, and publish findings in peer-reviewed journals. The annual goal is, on average, to have at least four papers in progress and at least two submitted for publication. Disseminate TMW research findings to broader audiences by presenting in select conferences and meetings of early childhood researchers, psychologists, and economists. Maintain existing TMW Center research collaborations with faculty at the University of Chicago, as well as other national and international faculty with whom the Center is partnering on projects. Participate in and contribute to the grant preparation process in a timely manner in close collaboration with the Co-Directors, potential Co-PIs, collaborators and consultants and the Grants and Contracts office. Participate in regularly scheduled TMW Center team meetings, lab meetings, and ‘papers’ meetings with Co-Director Suskind and weekly Econ meeting with Co-Director List.
Competencies: Excellent organizational, quantitative, and analytical skills with a high level of accuracy and sharp attention to detail required. Superior interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively with a wide range of individuals and constituencies in a diverse professional environment required. Ability to effectively manage a heavy workload, competing priorities, and tight deadlines required. A quick learner with the ability to initiate, organize, prioritize, and complete multiple, high-level projects; meet tight deadlines; and work effectively with minimal supervision in a fast-paced environment required. Strong computer skills including programming, ability to work with data sets, and data visualization ability required. Strong written and verbal communication skills required. Ability to work both independently and as a team member required.
Qualifications Before the start of employment, qualified applicants must have: Applicants must have a Ph.D. in Economics. Two years of postdoctoral experience and research within the field of economics. A microeconomist with experience in experimental and behavioral economics is preferred Strong expertise in education and health policy. Demonstrated ability to communicate research findings clearly to multiple audiences through oral presentations and written work. Experience in writing grant proposals, and a strong commitment to research preferred. We especially welcome applicants with technical knowledge or skills in: Knowledge of Stata, Python, Matlab, and/or R preferred. Knowledge of LaTeX required.
Application Instructions Applicants must apply online through the University of Chicago Academic Recruitment job board at https://apply.interfolio.com/190379. Applicants are required to submit: Resume/CV Cover Letter (include earliest available start date) Research statement Additionally, applicants are strongly encouraged to submit, as optional, up to three published or unpublished research papers. Screening of applications will continue until the position is filled or the search is closed.

In addition to teaching, the IP will advise and mentor undergraduate and masters students, organize student activities, contribute to recruitment and admissions of MA students and oversee and plan the curriculum under the direction of the Director of Undergraduate Studies and the Director of MA programs.
The terms and conditions of employment for this position are covered by a collective bargaining agreement between the Service Employees Union (SEIU) and the University.
This position is benefits-eligible. The University of Chicago offers a wide range of benefits programs and resources for eligible employees, including health, retirement, and paid time off. Information about the benefit offerings can be found in the Benefits Guidebook.
Qualifications Applicants must have a Ph.D. in Economics. Teaching experience with courses in applied economics, particularly pertaining to macroeconomics, OR statistics, data science, casual inference, and econometrics, with an emphasis on practical applications of the tools taught in these courses is required.
Consideration for the hiring level will be granted conditional on professional qualifications. The successful candidate will have outstanding in-person, written, and virtual communication skills and the ability to teach audiences with diverse backgrounds and with varying levels of knowledge about economics. Candidates should be comfortable teaching from introductory courses through courses at the master’s level.
Application Instructions Applicants must apply online at the University of Chicago’s Interfolio academic job board at: apply.interfolio.com/190053. Applicants are required to submit: 1) curriculum vitae, 2) teaching statement, 3) student evaluations, 4) two published or unpublished research papers, and 5) three letters of recommendation.

position.jp_full_text:
Join A World-Class Economics Team At UQ
The School of Economics at The University of Queensland (UQ) invites applications for two academic positions at Lecturer (Level B) or Senior Lecturer (Level C) level, in any field of economics.
As a teaching and research academic, you’ll join a vibrant, internationally recognised academic community. Whether you’re early in your academic career or ready to take the next step, this is an opportunity to build your global research profile and contribute to innovative teaching in one of Australia’s leading economics schools.
Note for US applicants: In the Australian academic system, a Lecturer is broadly equivalent to an Assistant Professor in the US, while a Senior Lecturer is a more senior appointment.
Why UQ?
As part of the UQ community, you will have the opportunity to work alongside the brightest minds, who have joined us from all over the world, and within an environment where interdisciplinary collaborations are encouraged. As part of our commitment to excellence in research and professional practice in academic contexts, we are proud to provide our staff with access to world-class facilities and equipment, grant writing support, greater research funding opportunities, and other forms of staff support and development.
The greater benefits of joining the UQ community are broad: from being part of a Group of Eight university, to recognition of prior service with other Australian universities, up to 26 weeks of paid parental leave, 17.5% annual leave loading, flexible working arrangements, access to exclusive internal-only vacancies, and genuine career progression opportunities via the academic promotions process.
Relocating from interstate or overseas? We may support you with obtaining employer-sponsored work rights and a relocation support package, however upfront costs will still be expected to be covered. You can find out more about life in Australia’s Sunshine State here.
For more information about this opportunity, please contact Professor Claudio Mezzetti at c.mezzetti@uq.edu.au.
For application queries, please contact Jenna Bachmann at talent@uq.edu.au stating the job reference number (R-69343) in the subject line.

position.jp_title: Tenure Track Nonmarket Strategy/Political Economy Position
position.jp_institution: The University of Texas at Austin
position.jp_full_text:
The Department of Business, Government & Society (BGS) at the University of Texas at Austin’s McCombs School of Business invites applications for an assistant professor (tenure track) position in nonmarket strategy/political economy effective August 16, 2027. We are particularly interested in candidates whose research focuses on global political economy, including but not limited to firms’ and industries’ roles in geopolitics/economics, trade, and resource/environmental economics.
The BGS department (https://www.mccombs.utexas.edu/departments/BGS) is an interdisciplinary group that teaches future leaders at all levels of McCombs’ curriculum how to recognize and respond to the political, social, legal, and ethical expectations that businesses face. BGS aims to contribute to important public policy debates in these and related areas through research that applies rigorous social science methods to relevant nonmarket strategy/political economy questions.
The school’s location in Austin is particularly attractive to faculty interested in connecting with a thriving business community and the Texas state government. For more details on the school and the department, please visit http://www.mccombs.utexas.edu/ and https://www.mccombs.utexas.edu/Departments/BGS. Finally, Austin is an outstanding place to live! See http://www.austintexas.org/visit/ for some of the many things that contribute to the high quality of life in Austin.
Qualifications:
The ideal candidate will possess a Ph.D. in economics, political science, or strategic management no later than the start date of the position and be prepared to publish in top outlets in these fields. The primary teaching responsibilities will require the candidate to contribute to the department’s offerings in international business at the undergraduate, MBA, and EMBA levels, as well as to help staff the department’s new undergraduate core class in nonmarket strategy.
Applicant Instructions:
Interested parties should submit the following: 1) a cover letter that includes brief statements of research and teaching interests, 2) a CV, 3) a job market paper, 4) three letters of recommendation, and, if available, 5) evidence of teaching effectiveness (e.g., sample syllabi and student evaluations). All applications submitted by Friday, September 25, 2026 will receive full consideration, although the search will continue until a suitable candidate is identified. UT-Austin uses Interfolio’s Faculty Search. Applicants to this position receive a free Dossier account and can send all application materials free of charge. The posting is available here: apply.interfolio.com/190563
Direct any inquiries to Timothy Werner (timothy.werner@mccombs.utexas.edu). The University of Texas at Austin is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
position.jp_keywords: Global political economy Firms’ roles Industries roles Geopolitics/economics Trade Resource economics Environmental economics

position.jp_full_text:
Description The McCombs School of Business at The University of Texas at Austin invites applications for a faculty position in Artificial Intelligence and Operations Management, beginning in Fall 2027. We seek candidates with a strong commitment to high-quality research and teaching who can contribute to our undergraduate and graduate courses in Artificial Intelligence and Operations Management. We are particularly interested in candidates who use rigorous empirical and data-driven methods to address problems in application domains such as revenue management, supply chains, healthcare, retailing, transportation and logistics, and technology and operations.
A successful candidate will be expected to establish an internationally recognized research program at The University of Texas at Austin, mentor graduate students, and teach at the undergraduate and graduate levels. The predominant mode of instruction and research is in person; accordingly, faculty appointed for employment shall reside in the proximate area of the work site for the duration of their appointment and be able to maintain a daily in-person schedule at the assigned work site.
The McCombs School of Business, with its top-ranked faculty and educational programs, offers a stimulating and collegial environment for innovative research and teaching. The school’s research centers, including centers focused on supply chain management, electronic commerce, entrepreneurship, marketing, and energy management, provide opportunities to collaborate with colleagues across disciplines and interact with a range of industry partners in Austin, throughout Texas, and nationally.
A background check will be conducted on applicants selected for the position prior to appointment.
Qualifications A Ph.D. (or very near completion) from an accredited institution is required by the start date of the appointment.
Application Instructions Applicants should submit a letter of interest, curriculum vitae, a job-market paper or other representative research manuscript, and a statement of research objectives and accomplishments. Three confidential letters of recommendation should also be submitted via Interfolio. Candidates with teaching experience should upload teaching evaluations.
At their discretion, applicants with prior faculty experience, such as current assistant or associate professors, may defer submission of recommendation letters during the initial application stage. Such candidates will be asked to provide references if selected as finalists. Additional materials may also be requested after the initial review of applications.
All materials should be submitted through Interfolio using the following link: apply.interfolio.com/194218
The application deadline is December 1, 2026. Applications received by October 15, 2026, will also be considered for interviews at the INFORMS Annual Meeting on November 1, 2026.
Please do not submit applications or updated materials via email.

The University is committed to a policy of equal opportunity for all persons and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, age, marital status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, disability, religion, or veteran status in employment, educational programs and activities, and admissions.

We are accepting applications for an Economist position in the Expert Analysis Division, Office of General Counsel, U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. As an Economist, you will be responsible for serving as an authority in economics and provide expert opinions, guidance, and direction to management, trial attorneys, and others in the analysis of employment discrimination cases.
Our team of PhD-level Economists within the Expert Analysis Division at EEOC conduct independent and objective analyses of employer-specific data to assess claims of discrimination in employment and testify as experts in court. We provide expert advice and advise legal staff on appropriate analytical methods, data requirements, and statistical techniques for case development and research efforts. A background in labor economics or a related microeconomic area is preferred for this position.
The position requires a duty station at Headquarters (in Washington, D.C.) or one of the 53 EEOC Field Offices (EEOC Field Offices | U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission).
The position will be at the GS-13 level with a promotion potential at GS-14. The start date is negotiable.

position.jp_section: Full-Time Nonacademic
position.jp_full_text:
Uber India's looking for economists with a passion for tackling hard problems with real-world impact. We are economists, statisticians, operations researchers, and computer scientists who combine theoretical insight with rigorous data analysis to expand the value created across Uber’s real-time marketplaces. Economists at Uber work on teams across the company in a variety of roles; we will match hires to roles best suiting their interests and expertise. Economists are central to our strategic decisions and algorithmic solutions. We're hiring economists at all experience levels for our Bengaluru-based team.
What You'll Do
Solve ambiguous business challenges by designing pricing, incentives, and subscription structures.
Model long-term consumer behavior and develop ML-driven optimizations for marketplace levers.
Design experiments (A/B, market-level); apply observational causal inference.
Develop novel data science methodologies and drive technical vision alongside cross-functional teams.
Present findings to business leaders to inform critical strategic decisions.
Qualifications
Basic: Ph.D. in Economics (or a related field) and programming proficiency.
Preferred: Ability to creatively approach business-relevant economic problems; foundational skills in SQL, R, Python, C, C++, or Java; expertise in experimental design and causal inference with observational data; and experience in algorithm prototyping.
position.jp_keywords: Industrial Organization Applied Microeconomics Data Science Machine Learning Econometrics Market Design Labor Economics Urban Economics

position.jp_full_text:
The UChicago/UCEMA joint initiative JILAEE accepts applications for two postdoctoral scholar positions from July 2027, or earlier on agreement.
JILAEE is a research center that is co-directed by Julio Elias (UCEMA) and John A. List (UChicago). Its mission is to promote the use of field experiments in Latin America, and to strengthen relationships between researchers, governments, and private organizations to advance the use of (experimental) economics. For more information: https://www.jilaee.org/
JILAEE postdoctoral scholars spend 2/3 of their time in Buenos Aires to establish new research partnerships, design and conduct field experiments, and strengthen their research pipeline before starting tenure track faculty positions. JILAEE postdocs spend 1/3 of their time at UChicago, and are closely integrated in John List's experimental economics group throughout the term of the postdoctoral position. The postdoctoral scholars are highly encouraged to start new projects and co-author on research papers with JILAEE affiliates and researchers in Latin America and the University of Chicago.
There are no teaching or administrative obligations. The term for the position is flexible and can be up to two years. Applicants with research interests in experimental economics, development economics, and/or behavioral economics and experience in conducting field experiments will be given priority.
position.jp_keywords: Field Experiments Behavioral Economics Latin America

position.jp_full_text:
The Department of Economics invites applications for two tenure-track positions, at the rank of Assistant Professor, beginning July 1, 2027. Outstanding candidates in all economic fields will be considered. We welcome candidates whose experience in teaching, research, or community service has prepared them to contribute to our commitment to diversity and excellence. A tenure-track position requires teaching at the Ph.D. level, original research, and superior teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels. Candidates should have a Ph.D. in Economics in hand by date of hire. A two-year contract for junior faculty is renewable upon successful performance of duties. Salaries for appointments depend upon qualifications. Applications will be accepted via the UC Recruit web site at https://recruit.apo.ucla.edu/JPF11328. This URL can be used to link directly to the listing for your recruitment. You can use this URL in job ads, postings, electronic mailings, and links on other websites. In order to receive full consideration, applications should be submitted by December 1, 2026.
The posted UC salary scales set the minimum pay determined by rank and/or step at appointment. See Table 3. The salary range for this position is $111,400 to $139,200. “Off-scale salaries” and other components of pay, i.e., a salary that is higher than the published system-wide salary at the designated rank and step, are offered when necessary to meet competitive conditions. A reasonable estimated salary range for this position is $200,00 to $230,000, inclusive of the salary scale and off-scale salary components. See campus compensation page for additional information.
The University of California is committed to creating and maintaining a community dedicated to the advancement, application, and transmission of knowledge and creative endeavors through academic excellence, where all individuals who participate in University programs and activities can work and learn together in a safe and secure environment, free of violence, harassment, bullying and other demeaning behavior, discrimination, exploitation, or intimidation. With this commitment as well as a commitment to addressing all forms of academic misconduct, UCLA conducts targeted employment reference checks for finalists to whom departments or other hiring units would like to extend formal offers of appointment into Academic Senate faculty positions. The targeted employment reference checks involve contacting the finalists' current and prior places of employment to ask whether there have been substantiated findings of misconduct that would violate the University's Faculty Code of Conduct. To implement this process, UCLA requires all applicants for Academic Senate faculty positions to complete, sign, and upload the form entitled "Authorization to Release Information" into RECRUIT as part of their application. If the applicant does not include the signed authorization to release information with the application materials, the application will be considered incomplete. As with any incomplete application, the application will not receive further consideration. The Department of Economics at Universidad del CEMA (www.ucema.edu.ar), Buenos Aires, Argentina, invites applications for an Assistant or Associate Professor position beginning August 2026, or later by agreement.
We seek an applied microeconomist with strong expertise in empirical methods and program evaluation, including randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental designs and cost-benefit analysis. We especially welcome candidates working in one or more of the following fields: law and economics; labor economics; poverty and inequality; health economics; human capital; public economics; behavioral economics; Economics of Crime; and managerial economics.

position.jp_full_text:
The School of Finance, Economics, and Government at Universidad EAFIT (Medellín, Colombia) invites applications for three tenure-track positions at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor. Starting dates are flexible, between January and August 2027. The School ranks second among Colombian universities in the IDEAS/RePEc ranking. Selected candidates join an interdisciplinary research and teaching team with close ties to financial institutions, governments, multilateral organizations, and civil society organizations.
Position 1 — Macroeconomics and Financial Systems. Training and research experience in one or more of: macrofinance and macroprudential policy; finance and development; investment and growth; misallocation and productivity; sovereign debt and bond markets; pension systems.
Position 2 — Markets and Financial Strategy. Training and research experience in one or more of: the industrial organization of energy markets; organizational economics (theory of the firm, personnel economics, corporate finance); the intersection of urban economics and real estate finance.
Position 3 — Public Administration. Research experience in one or more of: public finance; public administration modernization and digital government (GovTech); subnational government and multilevel governance; integrity and transparency. Candidates should also offer capacity for applied quantitative and comparative research and teaching experience in public administration, management, or new technologies for the public sector.
All positions require a PhD in a relevant discipline by the start date or shortly thereafter; a strong research agenda or a publication record for appointment at the Associate rank; and a commitment to teaching at the graduate and undergraduate levels. Proficiency in Spanish and English is required. Salaries are competitive at all ranks, with bonuses for publications, grants, and consultancy, and tenure-track faculty receive a permanent contract after a successful tenure review.
How to Apply. Apply through the JOE Application, indicating which position you are applying for. Submit a cover letter describing your research agenda and teaching experience, a CV, a job market paper or other evidence of scholarly production, and two letters of recommendation.
Timeline. Review of applications begins September 30, 2026, and continues until December 15, 2026.

Tenure-Track Faculty Position
General Public Policy and Administration: Policy Analysis, Public Administration and Management - Goldman School of Public Policy
The Goldman School of Public Policy at the University of California, Berkeley, invites applications for a tenure-track appointment to the faculty at the Assistant Professor rank in the area of policy analysis and/or governmental management and public administration.
Against the backdrop of a world with fractured institutional trust, increased social stratification and inequality, diverse populations, dispersed decision-making, media and informational fragmentation, political and governmental volatility, skepticism about evidence, and the growing use of AI, the Goldman School seeks a faculty member whose research considers the changing role of public policy analysis and/or the changing nature of governmental management.
The Goldman School encourages applications from scholars in a broad range of disciplines, including public policy, political science, economics, public affairs, sociology, psychology, business, and law, as well as data scientists with roots in computer science, schools of information, economics, and other fields, whose research engages with questions of public policy and/or public administration. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, the development or study of policy analysis methods, research on policy-analysis institutions, studies of bureaucracy, personnel management, organizational behavior, budgeting, procurement and logistics, program implementation, governmental performance, governmental decision-making, strategic thinking and planning, the use of AI in government, or methods for increasing democratic outreach, inclusion, and governmental trust. We welcome applications from researchers studying these topics in the United States and around the world.
The University of California, Berkeley is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, or protected veteran status.

Associate/Full Professor of Agricultural and Resource Economics
To address the diverse needs of California’s agricultural economy, the Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics in the College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences at the University of California, Davis is recruiting an Associate/Full Professor of Agricultural Economics. This is an academic year (9-month), tenured Associate/Full Professor position with a 20% Instruction and Research, and 80% Agricultural Experiment Station appointment.
The Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics seeks applicants for a faculty position focused on the challenges facing California’s farm economy. The appointee will develop a statewide applied research and outreach program addressing production costs and returns, the farm-level costs and effects of regulation, and management strategies that support profitability and long-term economic viability. The appointee will also lead UC Davis ARE’s Cost and Return Studies program, supervise research staff, work with funders and other stakeholders, and secure extramural support for the program’s core activities and methodological development. Teaching may include courses such as ARE 120, Agricultural Policy; ARE 138, International Commodity and Resource Markets; ARE 139, Futures and Options Markets; ARE 155, Operations Research and Management Science; master’s-level courses such as ARE 223 and ARE 271; and Ph.D.-level courses in applied methods and agricultural economics, including ARE 202B, ARE 202C, and ARE 231–233. The appointee will also advise and mentor undergraduate and graduate students.
This is an academic year (9-month), tenured Associate/Full Professor position with outreach/engagement, research, teaching and mentoring, and service responsibilities.
Required application materials include: 1) curriculum vitae including publication list, 2) up to three research papers or publications 3) statement of research accomplishments and future research plans, 4) statement of outreach accomplishments and philosophy, 5) up to three outreach papers or publications 6) statement of teaching and mentoring background 7) at least three recommendation letters, and 8) an Authorization Release Form. Additional inquiries should be directed to Professor Rachael Goodhue, Recruitment Advisory Committee Chair (regoodhue@ucdavis.edu).
As one of the country’s leading R1 institutions, UC Davis seeks candidates who have demonstrated outstanding accomplishments in outreach research, teaching, and inclusive excellence. The successful candidate will have an accomplished track record (calibrated to career stage) of outreach, research, teaching or service activities, and a clearly articulated vision of how their work at UC Davis will continue to contribute to the University’s mission of serving the needs of our diverse agricultural economy and stakeholders.
Applicants should submit materials via the following website: https://apptrkr.com/9836755. Additional inquiries can be directed to Rachael Goodhue (regoodhue@ucdavis.edu). UC San Diego is seeking applications for a postdoctoral fellow (2-year appointment) who aspires to become an independent academic researcher in the field of health economics and health policy, with a focus on drug use and abuse.
Position Description: The fellow will work closely with Dr. Yuyan Shi on multiple projects that (1) evaluate the impacts of drug policies, (2) examine neighborhood retail environments, and (3) assess market trends and product mix. Drugs of interest include cannabis, tobacco, and other licit and illicit drugs.
Qualifications: Applicants should hold a doctoral degree by Oct 2026 in public health or a social science discipline such as health economics, health policy, behavioral economics, health services, communication, or a related field. Ideal candidates will have strong quantitative skills, including experience analyzing large-scale population surveys and administrative data. Strong writing and communication skills are required. Experience in drug use and policy research is preferred. Demonstrated expertise in at least one of the following areas is an advantage: (1) analyzing sales or market data using advanced econometric methods, (2) structural modeling, or (3) machine learning.
position.jp_keywords: Health Economics Health Policy Behavioral Economics Drug Abuse Drug Policy

position.jp_full_text:
The California Policy Lab seeks a mid- or advanced-career researcher to design and conduct policy-relevant research on homelessness and health in partnership with state and local agencies. Our team works closely with policymakers and people with lived experience to develop research that informs solutions to homelessness.
Responsibilities: Conduct quantitative research using causal inference methods Publish reports and policy briefs for academic and policy audiences Write grant proposals and manage grant reporting Supervise and mentor junior research staff Partner with government agencies to build joint research agendas
Qualifications: Ph.D. in economics, public policy, statistics, or related field (or equivalent experience) Expertise in homelessness and/or health policy research Experience with large administrative datasets, especially Medicaid and health billing data Proficiency in Stata, R, Python, SQL, or similar statistical software Expertise in causal inference methodology Strong writing and communication skills Preferred: 5+ years of professional experience, supervisory experience, grant writing, and commitment to advancing racial equity.

position.jp_full_text: The Department of Economics at the University of California, Riverside, invites applications for a Visiting Assistant Professor of Economics. The appointment will be for one quarter (Fall 2026), beginning September 2026. Primary responsibilities will include teaching two graduate-level macroeconomics courses, specifically the first-year core sequence and a second-year elective in the Ph.D. program. The appointed candidate is expected to engage in scholarly and/or professional activities and participate in service to the department, college, university, and broader profession. Applicants must be ABD or have met the requirements for a Ph.D. in Economics or a closely related field by the start of the appointment. Successful candidates should have a proven record or strong potential for excellence in teaching graduate-level macroeconomics. The salary for a Visiting Assistant Professor is $14,016 per course or $28,032 for two courses, dependent on qualifications and experience. This is a negotiated rate of pay and is not dependent on a UC salary scale. Complete applications must include a cover letter of interest, a current CV, samples of research work, a teaching statement, teaching evaluations, and three letters of reference that are uploaded through the AP Recruit system. Review of applications will begin on August 26, 2026. To ensure full consideration, applications and supporting materials should be received by Wednesday, August 26, 2026. Applications and materials will be submitted using UCR’s online application system located at https://aprecruit.ucr.edu/JPF02323 The University of California is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified candidates will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or protected veteran status. Please note that the university does not provide visa sponsorship for this position.

position.jp_section: International: Other Academic (Visiting or Temporary)
position.jp_full_text:
The Janeway Institute at the Faculty of Economics, Cambridge University has a Postdoctoral Research Fellowship available. Eligible candidates include those who have recently been awarded a doctoral degree or expect to receive their degree by September 2027. The Fellowship is for a maximum of three years.
The Fellowship will be based at the Janeway Institute, which was created to develop new fundamental ideas, methods, and research which push the frontier of economics.
We welcome applications from researchers working on areas of economics related to transmission mechanisms and economic policy. This includes but is not limited to research into the contributions of firms and sectors in the aggregate economy; inquiries into how heterogeneity across households and firms shapes economic outcomes and contributes to economic growth; studies of the conduct and impact of monetary and fiscal policy in closed and open economies; and investigations of other economic factors that shape the economy and contribute to economic growth.
Successful candidates should demonstrate an ability to develop their own research ideas and indicate how they can contribute to the transmission mechanisms research group in Cambridge.
To apply, please follow this link: https://www.cam.ac.uk/jobs/janeway-institute-postdoctoral-research-fellowship-research-assistant-or-research-associate-fixed-jh50885

position.jp_section: US: Other Academic (Visiting or Temporary)
position.jp_full_text:
The Department of Economics in the Barry S. Miller College of Business at the University of Central Florida invites applications for an Economist-in-Residence and Visiting Instructor or Lecturer to help lead a new Initiative on Economic Decision Systems.
The Initiative examines how organizations design and manage decision systems in environments where economic reasoning, data, technology, and human judgment interact. Its centerpiece is the Economic Decision Systems Lab, where faculty, students, and organizational partners collaborate on applied decision problems. The Initiative supports the College's strategic emphasis on technology-enabled business transformation, industry engagement, and applied research.
This fixed-term position is designed for a dynamic, entrepreneurial individual interested in building new programs, developing partnerships, mentoring students, and translating economic thinking into organizational practice. Continued appointment beyond the initial term of up to 4 years may be considered based on success of the Initiative, evolution of organizational partnerships, and strategic priorities of the college. Success will be measured by the establishment of a functioning Lab with sustained external partnerships, a pipeline of applied projects, and a distinctive experiential learning program.
Minimum qualifications: A terminal degree (for a lecturer) or a master’s degree (for an instructor) in economics or a related discipline from an accredited institution at the time of application. Demonstrated experience applying economic reasoning and data analysis to organizational decision-making in data-rich environments.
Preferred qualifications: Experience applying economics to improve decisions in industry, consulting, government, financial services, technology, or other organizations. Experience leading applied projects at the intersection of economics, analytics, technology, and organizational design. Experience mentoring students or early-career professionals, or leading collaborative teams. Experience integrating human and artificial intelligence for organizational decision-making. A dynamic, entrepreneurial interest in developing partnerships and new programs. Ability and willingness to engage external organizations and help shape the direction of the Initiative.
Applications must be submitted electronically at the link below. In addition to the online application, applicants should upload (1) a cover letter describing how their experience aligns with the goals of the Initiative and the qualifications listed above, and (2) a curriculum vitae. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. Official transcripts (and, if applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) will be required before appointment.
position.jp_keywords: Economics

position.jp_full_text:
The University of Colorado Boulder invites applications for the position of Director of the Institute of Behavioral Science (IBS), a leading interdisciplinary research institute dedicated to advancing innovative social and behavioral science.
We seek an accomplished scholar with an outstanding record of research, teaching, and service that qualifies for appointment as Professor with tenure at CU Boulder. The successful candidate will have demonstrated administrative and research leadership, a strong commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration, and the ability to articulate and implement a strategic vision for a large, externally funded research institute.

The Director provides intellectual and administrative leadership, fosters interdisciplinary research and training, supports faculty and student development, strengthens partnerships with external stakeholders, and maintains an active, externally funded research program.
Candidates must hold a Ph.D. in a social or behavioral science or a closely related field. Review of applications will begin September 1, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. The anticipated start date is January 1, 2027.
For the complete position description and application instructions, please apply through the University of Colorado Boulder Jobs website.

position.jp_full_text:
The University of Delaware seeks an Embedded Behavioral Scientist for Conservation Delivery. The position will be based in the USDA NRCS Missouri State Office in Columbia, Missouri, while employed by the University of Delaware under the guidance of Kent D. Messer, Director of the Center for Behavioral and Experimental Agri-Environmental Research (CBEAR). The successful candidate will collaborate closely with USDA NRCS, Ducks Unlimited at both the Missouri and national levels, and a network of applied researchers to improve conservation program delivery through behavioral science.
This is a rare opportunity to help establish one of the first embedded behavioral science programs within USDA conservation delivery while contributing to applied research with national relevance.
Qualifications: Master's or Ph.D. in behavioral economics, economics, psychology, public policy, or a related field.
Appointment: Approximately a 2.5-year appointment with the opportunity for extension contingent upon funding. Competitive salary with excellent University of Delaware health and retirement benefits.
Application Process: Applications will be reviewed starting on September 30, 2026. Preferred start date is January 1, 2027, with the possibility of an earlier start for an exceptional candidate.
Applicants should submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, and contact information for three references to Dr. Kent Messer (messer@udel.edu).

position.jp_full_text:
The Department of Economics at the University of Houston invites applications for up to two positions at the tenure-track Assistant Professor level, tenured Associate Professor level, or tenured Full Professor level, to begin in Fall 2027. We will consider applicants in all fields but have a particular interest in candidates whose research and teaching are focused on macroeconomics.
The candidates are expected to conduct research to publish in leading economics journals, teach economics courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels, serve as a research mentor to doctoral students, and interact effectively with colleagues to support and enhance the department's intellectual atmosphere.
Candidates must possess a Ph.D. in Economics or are expected to complete their Ph.D. by August 2027. Applications must include: A cover letter. Curriculum vitae. Three or more reference letters. A job market paper.
Candidates may also include additional material they think is pertinent for the position (e.g., other research papers, research and teaching statements, teaching evaluations, etc.).
Review of candidates will begin November 1st, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. The department will conduct virtual first-round interviews, followed by in-person flyouts for selected candidates.
Salary and rank commensurate with experience.
The University of Houston is a Carnegie Tier One public research university with over 49,000 students. The Department of Economics is dedicated to producing top-flight research while training students in the latest techniques in economic analysis. Faculty members publish their work in the top journals of their fields, are vital contributors to prestigious associations and editorial boards, and regularly present their research papers at major institutions and conferences worldwide. The following website contains more information on the department: https://www.uh.edu/class/economics/
Application deadline: 04/30/2027
Please go to the UH Careers website to complete your online application: https://careers.uh.edu/jobs/assistant-associate-or-full-professor-economics-houston-texas-united-states
The names of your references will be submitted as part of your application, and they will be contacted directly by the University of Houston to provide their letters.
Employees are expected to have a home address in the state of Texas for the duration of their appointments.
Official transcripts are required for a faculty appointment and will be requested upon selection of the final candidates.
All positions at the University of Houston-System are security sensitive and will require a criminal history check. Individuals conducting research in critical infrastructure areas (i.e., communication infrastructure systems, cybersecurity systems, electric grid, hazardous waste treatment systems, and/or water treatment facilities) are subject to regular review to ensure the security and integrity of the research is maintained.
The University of Houston System and its universities are Equal Opportunity Institutions. Everyone is encouraged to apply.

The University of Kansas, School of Business invites applications for a full-time, academic-year tenure-track finance position at the assistant professor level. This position starts in Fall 2027. Salary and benefit package are competitive.
Candidates should have a Ph.D. in finance or a closely related field by August 18, 2027; demonstrate, or show evidence of high potential for, scholarship excellence through publications and working papers; and demonstrate, or show evidence of high potential for, teaching excellence. Areas of particular interest include corporate finance, financial institutions, international finance, investments, and risk management.
The University of Kansas School of Business offers undergraduate, master’s (full-time and online) and doctoral programs. In recent years, the School has experienced remarkable growth, expanding academic offerings with student enrollment approaching 5,000 students. The School of Business is located on KU’s main campus in Lawrence in Capitol Federal Hall, a 166,500 sq ft modern instructional facility with advanced classrooms, offices, and student resources. Lawrence is located 35 miles west of Kansas City in the Kansas River valley. For information about the University of Kansas, School of Business and living in Lawrence, see http://business.ku.edu/ and https://www.ku.edu/about-lawrence.
Candidates may apply online at http://www.employment.ku.edu/academic/33490BR. The letters of reference should be sent to busfncadmin@ku.edu. Screening of applicants will begin on September 15, 2026 and will continue until our applicant pool has been determined. Questions regarding the position may be addressed to Kevin Pisciotta at kpisciotta@ku.edu.
The University of Kansas prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, national origin, age, ancestry, disability status as a veteran, sexual orientation, marital status, parental status, gender identity, gender expression, and genetic information in the university's programs and activities. position.jp_full_text:
Title: Assistant Professor - Department of Economics Executive Area: Academic Affairs College/School/MBU: Social & Behavioral Sciences Department: Economics Work Location: Amherst Schedule: Full Time Work Arrangement: Hybrid
Job Summary The Department of Economics at the University of Massachusetts Amherst invites applications for an Assistant Professor appointment expected to start on September 1, 2027.
Essential Functions The Department of Economics at the University of Massachusetts Amherst invites applications for an Assistant Professor appointment expected to start on September 1, 2027.
Preference will be given to innovative analytical methods, both empirical and theoretical, in a core area such as microeconomics, industrial organization, international trade and finance, and economic history, although economists in all fields are encouraged to apply. UMass Economics has a history and commitment to fostering a wide range of alternative perspectives and rigorous analytic methods for addressing economic challenges in innovative ways.
The teaching load is 2/2. Candidates will be judged on their scholarly research, as well as high quality and enthusiastic teaching. A completed Ph.D. in Economics or a closely related field is required by time of appointment. Current or previous external funding, or experience seeking external grants, is a plus.
Under exceptional circumstances, highly qualified candidates at other ranks may receive consideration.
Minimum Qualifications A Ph.D. in Economics, or a closely related field by the start date of the appointment. Candidates will be judged on their scholarly research, as well as high quality and enthusiastic teaching.
Additional Details The Economics faculty members at UMass Amherst work in diverse areas, from heterodox economics, such as Marxian, Post-Keynesian, Neo-Ricardian, Institutionalist, feminist, and stratification economics, to mainstream approaches such as applied microeconomics, economics and philosophy, and general equilibrium theory. The faculty studies economic theory and applied economics related to multiple dimensions of human well-being and social welfare; how economic opportunities are generated and distributed in society; the interplay between power and institutions and between economic behavior and the performance of the economy; and the importance of race, class, and gender. The Department is committed to fostering a diverse faculty, student body, and curriculum. This position is subject to final budgetary and administrative approval.
Working Conditions Work is performed in a standard office or indoor university environment and involves minimal physical exertion.
Work Schedule and Work Arrangement This position is expected to start on 9/1/27.
Salary Information The University of Massachusetts Amherst expects to pay within an approximate range between $79,350 and $168,797 for this position. Please note:
The low-end of the pay range in all faculty searches at the University of Massachusetts Amherst is the minimum salary for the rank included in the collective bargaining agreement between the University and the Massachusetts Society of Professors, UMass Amherst/MTA/NEA.
The high-end of the pay range reflects an increase above the median of salaries at this rank within the department for faculty who may have multiple years of faculty experience. The specific pay for this position will be determined by the University based on consideration of all relevant factors, including faculty rank and required relevant certifications, when and if it decides to extend an offer of employment.
Special Instructions for Applicants Applicants must apply through the UMass online application system unless they are unable to do so. Applicants should submit:
1. A letter of interest addressed to Professor Mwangi wa Gĩthĩnji, Chair, Department of Economics (Crotty Hall, 412 North Pleasant Street, Amherst, MA 01002, USA). 2. Curriculum vitae. 3. One recent research paper. 4. Evidence of teaching effectiveness. 5. Names and contact information for three references who are willing to submit letters upon request through the UMass online application system. 6. A teaching statement that discusses: the candidate’s skills, experiences and commitment to teaching and mentoring diverse and historically underrepresented student populations.
Review of applications will begin on November 15, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. Preference will be given to applications received on or before November 15, 2026. Selected candidates will be interviewed remotely beginning in December 2026, with campus visits beginning after January 11, 2027.
Questions can be addressed to hiring@econs.umass.edu.
This position will remain open for the time period required by any applicable collective bargaining agreement and will continue until a suitable candidate pool is identified. Interested applicants are strongly encouraged to apply early.

position.jp_full_text:
The Molasky Family Department of Economics and Real Estate in the Lee Business School at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas invites applications for a tenure-track Lee Professorship of Economics with an emphasis in Real Estate and/or Urban Economics at the assistant or associate professor level. Preference will be given to candidates qualified for appointment at the advanced assistant professor or associate professor rank who have demonstrated the ability to publish high-quality research in real estate and/or urban economics. The department seeks a scholar whose research agenda will complement and extend existing departmental strengths and who demonstrates the ability to collaborate across the Lee Business School’s Centers of Excellence. In particular, the ideal candidate will be positioned to engage with and contribute to the Lied Center for Real Estate’s research and policy programs. Responsibilities of the position include conducting significant scholarly research leading to high-quality refereed publications in economics and real estate. Additional responsibilities include contributing to the Lee Business School’s research culture, and providing service to the department, school, university, and profession. The ideal candidate will also be expected to teach classes in service of the real estate degree offered by the department.
Salary and faculty support: The salary for this position is competitive with similarly situated institutions. The Lee Professorship provides additional support in the form of stipend and additional travel/research funds. See published salary tables for economics professors by rank (https://www.unlv.edu/hr/compensation-and-classification/academic).
Qualifications: This position requires a Ph.D. in Economics, Finance, or related disciplines from an accredited college or university as recognized by the United States Department of Education and/or the Council on Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) and the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB). Applicants for appointment at the Assistant Professor level should demonstrate strong promise of sustained, high-quality research in real estate, urban economics, and related fields, including the potential to publish in leading academic journals. Assistant Professor of Practice in Finance University of North Carolina Wilmington
Posting Details
Position Title Assistant or Associate Professor of Finance College Cameron School Business - 312 College Dept/School Economics and Finance - 31250 Vacancy Number 16F-788 Position Number 664 Location of Workplace Main UNCW Campus
Brief Summary of Work for this Position The Department of Economics and Finance at the University of North Carolina Wilmington invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position in Finance at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor. We seek collegial and engaged scholars who will contribute to the department's mission through excellence in research, teaching, and service. The anticipated start date is August 2027.
The successful candidate will demonstrate a strong commitment to scholarly research, with an established or emerging research agenda in any area of finance. The candidate should also possess the ability to deliver high-quality, engaging instruction at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. Teaching responsibilities may include courses in the Bachelor of Science in Business Administration (Finance concentration), Master of Business Administration (MBA), International MBA (IMBA), and Master of Science in Finance (MSF) programs.
UNCW's Master of Science in Finance curriculum is closely aligned with the Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) Program. Accordingly, candidates who hold the CFA charter or are actively progressing toward the credential are especially encouraged to apply
Minimum Education and Experience Requirements Ph.D. in Finance, Real Estate, or related field from an AACSB-accredited school. NOTE: ABDs with an expected conferral date before August 1, 2027, are encouraged to apply. ABD candidates with a Ph.D. conferred by August 1, 2027, can anticipate an initial appointment as Assistant Professor.
Selected candidates with a Ph.D. nearly completed (ABD, not conferred by August 1, 2027) can anticipate an initial appointment as Lecturer at a reduced salary for a one-year fixed-term appointment. Degree verification must be provided before the end of the one-year fixed-term contract, and the candidate will be appointed to the rank of assistant professor with commensurate compensation beginning July 1 of the following academic year.
Preferred Education, Knowledge, Skills & Experience CFA charter or progress towards CFA is preferred.
Required Certifications or Licensure
Primary Function of Organizational Unit The Department of Economics and Finance at the University of North Carolina Wilmington, located in the vibrant coastal city of Wilmington, North Carolina, offers four Bachelor of Science in Business Administration concentrations: Economics, Finance, Financial Technology (FinTech), and Real Estate. The department also administers the Bachelor of Arts in Economics and the Master of Science in Finance programs. In addition, faculty play an integral role in supporting both the Master of Business Administration (MBA) and the International MBA, a joint program offered in collaboration with our international partner universities.
The department fosters an engaging and experiential learning environment through student organizations, competitive academic opportunities such as the College Fed Challenge and CFA Institute Research Challenge, the student-managed investment fund, undergraduate honors research, and other high-impact learning experiences. Faculty are equally committed to advancing scholarship, with a growing research portfolio and a strong culture of collaboration that enhances teaching, research, and service.
College/School Information UNCW boasts a beautiful 661-acre wooded campus with approximately 16,500 students and is one of the fastest growing institutions in the University of North Carolina system. The Cameron School of Business is AACSB accredited and serves more than 2200 business majors, including graduate students in the PMBA, EMBA, M.S. in Accounting, International MBA, M.S in Business Analytics, M.S. in Finance and Investments, and M.S. in Computer Science and Information Systems programs.
The Wilmington metropolitan area comprises approximately 225,000 people and features a thriving port, business community, and tourism industry. Bordered by both the Atlantic Ocean and the Cape Fear River, Wilmington offers the best in coastal living.
University Information The University of North Carolina Wilmington, the state's coastal university, is dedicated to the integration of teaching, mentoring, research and service. Widely acknowledged for its world-class faculty and staff and continuously recognized at a national level for scholarly excellence and affordability, UNCW offers a powerful academic experience that stimulates creative inquiry and critical thinking.
A public institution with nearly 18,000 students, UNCW offers a full range of baccalaureate- and graduate-level programs, as well as doctoral degrees in educational leadership, marine biology, nursing practice and psychology; and many distance learning options, including clinical research, an accelerated RN-to-BSN program, an Executive M.B.A. program structured for working professionals, and the nation's only bachelor's degree program focused on coastal engineering.
The university's efforts to advance research and scholarly activities have earned UNCW the elevated designation of “Doctoral Universities: High Research Activity” institution (R2 University) by the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education.
UNCW has been part of the University of North Carolina System since 1969.
EEO Statement UNCW does not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of his or her race, sex (such as gender, gender identity, marital status, childbirth, and pregnancy), age, color, national origin (including ethnicity), religion, disability, sexual orientation, political affiliation, veteran status, military service member status, genetic information, or relationship to other university constituents – except where sex, age, or ability represent bona fide educational or occupational qualifications or where marital status is a statutorily established eligibility criterion for State funded employee benefit programs.
Eligibility for Employment Final candidates are subject to criminal & sex offender background checks. Some vacancies also require credit or motor vehicle checks. UNC Wilmington participates in E-Verify. Federal law requires all employers to verify the identity and employment eligibility of all persons hired to work in the United States.
Number of Openings Multi-Positions
Special Notes to Applicants Prior to the official appointment to the university, the candidate(s) selected for hire must be able to demonstrate eligibility to teach assigned courses by successfully meeting the credentialing requirements based on official transcripts and other documentation as required.
Please note that a minimum of three professional references are required for all applications.
Position Type Permanent Job Posting Date 08/11/2026 Job Close Date 09/17/2026
To apply, visit https://apptrkr.com/9758800

position.jp_full_text:
The Department of Economics in the Belk College of Business at UNC Charlotte is seeking to fill a Clinical Professor position. The position involves both teaching and administrative responsibilities as Director of the newly established North Carolina Economic Impact Center. The candidate will be on a reduced teaching load of four sections during the academic year due to the Director duties. Specific courses taught will be determined in consultation with the Department Chair.
The Director of the North Carolina Economic Impact Center will be responsible for administrative oversight of the Center. The primary purpose of the Center is to engage with industry and community leaders in the greater Charlotte region and conduct economic analyses by securing external funding.
Responsibilities for this position include sufficient academic and/or other professional activities to meet the Belk College Faculty Qualification Standards (https://belkcollege.charlotte.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/953/2026/08/BCOB-Policy-on-Qualified-Faculty-Status-Fall-2026.pdf). Will also engage in appropriate service activities in the Department, College, University, and Charlotte community.
Qualifications UNC Charlotte gives primary consideration to the earned master's and/or terminal degree in the teaching discipline or a related discipline.
Department Preferred Education, Skills, and Experience: PhD in Economics or related field. At least five years of experience at an executive level providing economic analysis of business or government policy. Demonstrated knowledge of economic impacts on the Charlotte, North Carolina, or greater Carolinas region.
Application Instructions & Process To ensure full consideration, please submit all required application materials. Applications must be submitted electronically at https://jobs.charlotte.edu/postings/70249 and include a cover letter and current CV. If available, applicants should submit evidence of teaching effectiveness. Finalists will be asked to forward official transcripts, three letters of reference, and other supportive materials as requested by the Search Committee. The candidate chosen for this position will be required to provide an official transcript of their highest earned degree and will be subject to a criminal background check.
About the College: The Belk College of Business at UNC Charlotte is North Carolina’s urban research business school, advancing knowledge, innovation, and service. Through an inclusive culture and strong regional partnerships, we prepare ethical, critical-thinking, globally aware leaders while driving research that shapes business theory, policy, and practice for a changing world.
As an EOE/AA employer and an advanced institution that strives to create an academic climate in which the dignity of all individuals is respected and maintained, the University of North Carolina at Charlotte encourages applications from all underrepresented groups.

Assistant Teaching Professor Of Economics
R0011104 Tampa
If you are a current University of Tampa student, please search for and apply to student jobs https://www.ut.edu/about-ut/university-services/human-resources/employment-opportunities via Workday. Job applications for current students will not be considered if submitted through the external career center.
Position Details
The Department of Economics at University of Tampa's Sykes College of Business invites applicants for a full-time, non-tenure track, Assistant Teaching Professor of Economics position to start in Fall 2027. Applicants with a Ph.D. in Economics will be given preference. A demonstrated commitment to teaching excellence is required. The applicant will also be expected to maintain an active research agenda and participate in service activities. The successful applicant will teach Principles of Macroeconomics or Principles of Microeconomics in our undergraduate program. The opportunity exists to teach other courses that match the applicant's interests. The teaching load is 3 courses (typically a single prep) per semester.
Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled.
All required documents listed below should be uploaded to the attachment box at the bottom of the "My Experience" page of the application before continuing through the application.
1. Cover Letter
2. Curriculum Vitae
3. Academic Writing Example
4. Copy of Teaching Evaluations (include a summary table)
5. Statement of Teaching Philosophy
6. Name and Contact Information of References
Reference Letters
Three reference letters from external providers are required. Please have the reference provider email the reference letter to Employment@ut.edu to include your name and the position you applied for in the email subject line.
The University of Tampa is a medium-sized, comprehensive, residentially-based private institution of more than 11,000 undergraduate and graduate students. The University is ideally situated on a beautiful 110-acre campus next to the Hillsborough River, adjacent to Tampa's dynamic central business district, which is a growing, vibrant, diverse metropolitan area. UTampa reflects this vibrancy; with 30 consecutive years of enrollment growth UTampa boasts 260 student organizations, a multicultural student body from 50 states and more than 100 countries, and "Top Tier" ranking in U.S. News and World Report.
The University delivers challenging and high-quality educational experiences to a diverse group of learners. The University has a strong core curriculum rooted in the liberal arts, an enduring commitment to internationalization that has garnered the Senator Paul Simon Award, and a practical, experiential approach to learning. The University offers more than 200 areas of study, including majors in our colleges of Arts and Letters, Business, Natural and Health Sciences and Social Sciences, Math and Education, 18 master's programs, and 3 professional doctoral programs.
The Sykes College of Business is AACSB accredited, employs over 100 full-time faculty members, and includes three centers and two institutes: Center for Ethics, TECO Energy Center for Leadership, John P. Lowth Entrepreneurship Center, Naimoli Institute for Business Strategy and Institute for Sales Excellence. The College occupies the state of the art Sykes College of Business building, housing the College's undergraduate and graduate students. The Sykes College of Business full-time MBA program is consistently listed as one of Bloomberg Businessweek's best graduate business schools and is ranked as one of the top 25 best value schools by Business Insider. The Economics Department is home to 19 full-time faculty members. The department offers a B.A. degree, a B.S. degree, and a minor, and it supports an active honors society for majors and minors.
The University of Tampa is an equal opportunity employer dedicated to excellence through diversity and does not discriminate on the basis of age, race, sex, disability, sexual orientation, national origin, religion, marital status, gender identity, veteran status, or any other non-job related criteria. The University of Tampa recognizes the importance of a multicultural community of students, faculty, and staff who seek to advance our commitment to diversity. The University invites applications from underrepresented groups and those who have academic experiences with diverse populations.
Submission Guidelines
To receive full consideration for a faculty appointment with The University of Tampa, please be sure to upload documents as required for this position at time of application submission. Once your application has been submitted, no changes may be made. Required documents should be submitted in the attachment box at the bottom of the "My Experience" page of the application before continuing through the application. Note: A maximum of five (5) documents may be attached to your application. If more than five (5) documents are required, please combine the additional documents into a single attachment so that you may continue through the application process.
Background Check Requirements
Finalists may be required to submit to a criminal background check.
To apply, visit https://apptrkr.com/9870510.

The Division of Quantitative Analysis of Markets and Organizations (QAMO) in the David Eccles School of Business at the University of Utah seeks candidates for a full-time, career- line faculty (lecturer) position in business economics. A successful candidate will hold a Ph.D. in economics (or a related field) with evidence of teaching undergraduate- and/or graduate-level courses in business economics. Depending on experience, lecturers can hold the rank of instructor, assistant professor, associate professor or professor.
Lecturers are non-tenure track faculty whose primary responsibility is teaching classes and advising students. Beyond this primary responsibility, all faculty in the David Eccles School of Business should sustain long-term currency and relevancy in their field of teaching; this may appear as scholarly activities and professional engagement within the field. The QAMO Division currently teaches the business core to all David Eccles School of Business students, the electives and core courses for the QAMO undergraduate major, as well as courses in the Eccles Business School’s MBA and PhD programs.
Applicants must have a record of successful teaching relevant to QAMO’s needs. We are especially interested in applicants with a demonstrated commitment to student-centered learning. This is an in-person position based in Salt Lake City, Utah. A strong candidate must able to develop elective courses for the QAMO major, oversee teaching assistants, and coordinate activities with other instructors.
The David Eccles School of Business is a world-class business school with a rich history of excellence in education and research. The University of Utah has recently announced an intention to form a School of Economics, bringing together faculty from the QAMO Division in the David Eccles School of Business and the Economics Department in the College of Social and Behavioral Sciences. The successful candidate will help shape a growing, newly integrated community of economists with opportunities to collaborate across business and social science perspectives and build innovative programs. Salaries and teaching loads are competitive with top economics departments and business schools, and the fringe benefits are excellent.
The QAMO Division is committed to removing barriers for all individuals, including those traditionally encountered by individuals from underrepresented groups; strives to recruit faculty who will further enhance our breadth; and makes every attempt to support their academic, professional, and personal success while they are here.
Applications will be accepted until October 9, 2026 or until position is filled.

position.jp_title: Assistant Professor of Public Policy (Market-Based Solutions to Societal Challenges)
position.jp_department: La Follette School of Public Affairs
position.jp_full_text:
The La Follette School of Public Affairs (LFS) seeks to hire a scholar whose research examines how market-based institutions, competitive structures, and incentive-compatible policy design can address major societal challenges. The successful candidate will conduct theoretically grounded and empirically rigorous research on the role of markets in domains traditionally shaped by public policy, regulation, or collective action problems.
We are particularly interested in scholars who analyze how prices, property rights, competition, decentralized information, and institutional design affect outcomes in areas such as:
Education/school finance and school choice Financial regulation and capital markets Housing supply and land-use reform Technology policy and innovation markets Transportation and infrastructure finance International trade and tariffs State and local economic development Climate and environmental policy (e.g., carbon pricing, cap-and-trade systems) Energy markets and grid reform Agricultural policy and food systems
The candidate may be an economist, political scientist, public policy scholar, legal scholar, or affiliated social scientist whose work engages deeply with the economic logic of markets and institutional design. We welcome scholars using diverse methodological approaches, including structural modeling, reduced-form econometrics, field experiments, institutional analysis, and political economy frameworks.
The successful candidate will contribute to teaching in public policy analysis, microeconomics for policy, regulatory policy, and sector-specific policy courses. They will strengthen LFS’s capacity to train students to evaluate when markets succeed, when they fail, how policy can improve their functioning, and how government failure represents an omnipresent risk.
Situated at the heart of UW-Madison, the College of Letters & Science (L&S) serves as home to 39 academic departments and numerous research centers, including the La Follette School of Public Affairs.
The successful applicant will be responsible for ensuring eligibility for employment in the United States on or before the effective date of the appointment. University sponsorship is not available for this position.
Madison is the state's capital city and is well known for offering a small town feel in a medium-sized city. It is a great place to raise a family and offers an ideal combination of natural beauty, stimulating cultural events, outstanding schools and outdoor recreation.
The successful candidate will advance the educational mission of the College of Letters & Science that values, prioritizes, and actualizes evidence-based and student-centered teaching and student mentoring. They will contribute to an environment that fosters engagement and a sense of belonging for faculty, staff, students and members of the broader community.
The successful candidate, as a member of the College of L&S, will proactively contribute to, support, and advance the college’s commitment to excellence among all aspects of their teaching, mentoring, research, and service.
In the College of Letters & Science, we provide a liberal arts education that is both broad and deep through excellent, empathic teaching. We hire faculty who are interested in pursuing difficult questions, making new discoveries, and making an impact in their field. We reward excellent teaching and classroom innovation, and we are committed to shared governance. Learn more about the L&S mission on our webpage: https://ls.wisc.edu/about/mission.
Key Job Responsibilities: The La Follette School of Public Affairs (LFS) seeks to hire a scholar whose research examines how market-based institutions, competitive structures, and incentive-compatible policy design can address major societal challenges. The successful candidate will conduct theoretically grounded and empirically rigorous research on the role of markets in domains traditionally shaped by public policy, regulation, or collective action problems.
