The U.S. Census Bureau anticipates multiple job openings for economists. The Census Bureau provides an excellent environment for empirically-oriented economists to use confidential microdata on businesses and households, linked employer-employee data, and administrative records from federal and state agencies to conduct research on a wide range of topics. These topics include business dynamics (productivity, trade, entrepreneurship, innovation); labor dynamics (employment, earnings, education, worker flows); income measurement (income inequality, income mobility, taxation, poverty, program participation); health (disability, insurance markets, mortality); household dynamics (family structure, migration, fertility); privacy and disclosure avoidance; and environmental and climate economics.
Economists' activities include presenting analytical and methodological research at professional conferences; publishing in scholarly journals; writing descriptive reports for the public; maintaining and improving data collection; and responding to inquiries from Congress, the press, and the public on topics of interest. Experience with firm-, household-, and/or industry-level data is especially valued, as are skills in data manipulation, analysis, and big data techniques. U.S. citizenship is required. Positions are subject to budgetary approval. The Census Bureau is an equal opportunity employer. Please submit materials using the JOE application. position.jp_full_text:
Position Summary
The Council of Economic Advisers seeks a Staff Economist to lead supply chain analysis across the nation's most critical and strategically vulnerable sectors. The role combines applied microeconomic and trade analysis with hands-on supply chain mapping—tracing where critical goods and their upstream inputs actually originate—and modeling how economic, trade, and procurement tools can shift sourcing toward the United States and partner nations.
The portfolio spans four priority areas: pharmaceuticals (finished drugs, active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), and key starting materials (KSMs)); semiconductors (with an emphasis on legacy/mature-node "foundational" chips); batteries and drones (cells, components, and the unmanned aircraft supply base); and critical minerals (extraction and, critically, processing and refining). A common analytical toolkit applies across all four: identify single-source vulnerabilities, distinguish direct from indirect exposure, and design economic levers to diversify supply.
This is a high-impact position for an economist who can move fluently between rigorous quantitative work and concrete policy design, and who is comfortable briefing senior officials on time-sensitive questions. ________________________________________
Key Responsibilities
Supply chain mapping and dependency analysis (across all priority sectors)
Build and maintain an evidence base on where critical goods and their upstream inputs originate, identifying single-source and country-concentration risks. Distinguish extraction/assembly from the true chokepoints, which often sit midstream—e.g., mineral processing and refining, mature-node foundry capacity, cell and cathode/anode manufacturing, and API/KSM synthesis. Integrate data from customs and import records, HS/HTS-level trade flows, FDA establishment registrations, foundry capacity by node and geography, and commercial supply chain sources to quantify concentration (e.g., HHI, single-country shares) and map vulnerabilities. Develop criticality metrics (defense and clinical relevance, substitutability, shortage/disruption history) and resilience metrics (geographic diversification, domestic capacity, inventory, stockpiles).
Sector-specific focus areas
Pharmaceuticals: finished-drug, API, and KSM sourcing; shortage risk. Semiconductors: legacy/mature-node chips embedded in autos, defense systems, medical devices, appliances, and grid hardware; risks from non-market capacity expansion and price suppression. Batteries and drones: lithium-ion cells and components, cathode/anode and precursor materials, and the unmanned aircraft (UAS) supply base, including secure-component and trusted-supplier considerations. Critical minerals: rare earths, lithium, cobalt, nickel, graphite, gallium, germanium and similar.
Policy tool analysis
Model the cost, feasibility, and likely supply response of economic and procurement levers, including trade remedies, Buy American and domestic-content preferences and penalties, federal procurement preferences and restrictions, advance purchase and offtake commitments, stockpiling, and targeted onshoring/ally-shoring incentives. Estimate effects on prices, availability and shortage risk, domestic manufacturing investment, and downstream costs; assess budgetary impact, unintended consequences, and gaming risks. Conduct cost-benefit and trade-off analysis weighing resilience gains against consumer-price and fiscal effects.
Partner-country and friend-shoring strategy
Analyze opportunities to diversify supply with allied and partner nations, including the economic case for ally-shoring of upstream production and processing. Assess how trade preferences, joint procurement, coordinated incentives, and partnership frameworks could stand up trusted alternative suppliers and shared stockpiles.
Briefing and inter-agency work
Produce memos, charts, and briefing materials. Support inter-agency analysis with partners. ________________________________________
Qualifications
Required
Advanced degree in economics or a closely related quantitative field (PhD preferred; exceptional candidates with a master's and strong relevant experience considered). Demonstrated applied skills in microeconomics, industrial organization, and/or international trade. Strong empirical and data skills (e.g., Stata, R, or Python) and the ability to work with messy real-world trade, customs, regulatory, and industry datasets. Ability to translate technical analysis into clear, decision-ready writing for non-economist principals.- Capacity to work quickly and accurately under deadline pressure on sensitive policy questions.
Preferred
Familiarity with one or more priority sectors: pharmaceutical manufacturing and the API/KSM value chain; semiconductor manufacturing and the mature-node landscape; battery and UAS supply chains; or critical minerals extraction and processing. Knowledge of U.S. trade- and industrial-policy instruments. Experience with supply-chain, network, or concentration analysis. Prior government, think tank, or inter-agency experience.
position.jp_keywords: Supply Chains International Trade

Windfall Trust is hiring a fully remote Scenarios & Modeling Economist to build and own its quantitative modeling capability, acting as the technical authority behind everything the organization publishes — choosing methods, assembling data, writing or directing code, and defending results to external economists, peer reviewers, and government analysts. The immediate focus is a scenario modeling platform that translates narrative AI futures into quantified economic parameters, propagates them through household microdata, and produces distributional and fiscal results: who loses income, by how much, what it costs the fiscal system, and how policy responses perform under each scenario. This is a build role — Windfall has no existing modeling infrastructure, so the hire will make foundational methodological choices from scratch, with scope expanding over time to other modeling work (indices, macro shock generators, fiscal costing) as needs evolve.
Responsibilities include designing the platform's economic primitives, mapping shocks onto occupations, simulating and costing policy responses (transfer programs, capital taxation, social insurance), co-authoring publications, and setting standards for reproducibility.
Strong candidates are senior economists with range across quantitative modeling approaches, comfortable defending technical choices externally, with an advanced degree and 5+ years of applied modeling experience.

Windfall Trust is hiring a fully remote Lead Economist to own its core research products and serve as the technical authority behind everything the organization publishes.
The role covers the full research lifecycle - methodological design, data and analysis, drafting, external review, and defending results to treasuries, central banks, and academic economists. Work spans Windfall's flagship products: the Policy Atlas, an upcoming Preparedness Map (assessing countries' AI economic exposure and absorption capacity), and a Scenarios Lab translating AI futures into distributional and fiscal outcomes. Responsibilities include designing cross-country index methodology, analyzing labor market resilience, assessing fiscal and welfare system resilience across income levels, costing policy responses, and authoring publications for government and institutional audiences. Windfall's research infrastructure is young, so the role involves making foundational methodological choices while working directly with the CEO and Director of Research.
Strong candidates are senior economists with a range of expertise across labor economics, development economics, fiscal/welfare policy, or quantitative modeling, comfortable being the most technical person in the room and accountable when external experts push back. Requirements: an advanced degree, 8+ years of applied research or policy experience, demonstrated senior-level work in at least two relevant fields, and a track record of methodology surviving external scrutiny.

position.jp_full_text:
The Economics and Management School at Wuhan University (https://ems.whu.edu.cn/English.htm) and The Institute for Advanced Study at Wuhan University (https://ias.whu.edu.cn/English.htm), China, invite applications for full-time, tenure-track or tenured positions at all levels beginning in Fall 2027. We are interested in all fields but candidates who have strong background in Insurance, Macroeconomics, Empirical Industrial Organization, Econometrics, and Finance are especially preferable.
To apply for assistant professor position at the Economics and Management School, a candidate needs to have a top field journal publication. For candidates specializing in Insurance or Risk Management, the publication requirement is somewhat flexible, and outstanding candidates without top field publications but with strong pipelines may also be considered. Junior candidates without publications are encouraged to apply for the postdoc positions. To apply for associate or full professor positions, candidates must demonstrate excellent publication records.
To apply for tenured associate or full professor positions at the Institute for Advanced Study, a new pilot program of the tenure-track system at Wuhan University, candidates should have qualifications comparable to those for similar positions at top-tier universities. Special support will be provided by the university in terms of compensation, research fund, teaching, and Ph.D supervision.
All candidates should be committed to teaching and research excellence. Compensation packages are highly competitive and commensurate with qualification and positions.
Application will only be accepted online via JOE (https://www.aeaweb.org/joe). Your application should include the following (all in PDF format): cover letter, curriculum vitae, job market paper, three letters of recommendation (sent separately by referees). Applicants who apply for tenured associate or full professor positions may arrange recommendation letters after being shortlisted and requested. Applications will be considered till the positions are filled, but applications received by November 10, 2026 will be guaranteed interviews before the 2027 AEA meetings. Please indicate clearly in your cover letter whether you apply to the Economics and Management School or the Institute for Advanced Study. Inquiries can be addressed to econrecruit@whu.edu.cn.
Wuhan University (WHU), with 130 years of history, is one of the top ten research-oriented universities in China and among the top 90 worldwide in US News and top 122 worldwide in THE in 2025. As the largest school at WHU, Economics and Management School (EMS) has a long-standing reputation for high-quality teaching and research in business and economics and has been accredited by three major international accreditation institutions (AMBA, EQUIS, and AACSB). Wuhan is a fast-growing, vibrant, large city with rich urban amenities, affordable housing, and high quality of life.

position.jp_section: International: Full-Time Academic (Permanent, Tenure Track or Tenured)
position.jp_department: Paula and Gregory Chow Institute for Studies in Economics
position.jp_full_text:
Job Description and Qualification Paula and Gregory Chow Institute for Studies in Economics (Chow Institute) invites applications for either tenure-track or tenured full-time faculty positions in the upcoming academic year, starting in September 2027. Any field. Our preferred areas of specializations are – but are not limited to – econometrics, statistics and data science, in addition to economics, and finance. Junior candidates are expected to have a Ph.D. degree by August 2027 and show evidence of promising research ability. Senior candidates must have a Ph.D. degree and a demonstrably strong research record. The Chow Institute offers competitive salary and benefit package, along with other benefits, including housing subsidies and research support.
About Professor Gregory Chow (Prepared by Professor Ben Bernanke, Chair of the Department of Economics, Princeton University, in May 2001.)
Gregory C. Chow is the Class of 1913 Professor of Political Economy Emeritus at Princeton University. He has been a major figure in econometrics and applied economics. Every beginning econometrics student learns the "Chow test", a statistical test for structural change in a regression. However, Gregory's work extends far beyond his eponymous test. He was a major figure in the postwar flowering of econometrics, and his applied work included important research in microeconomics, macroeconomics, and development economics (particularly in reference to Southeast Asia).
Gregory has become a towering figure in economic transition and economics education in Asia. He played an important role in the transformation of the economy of mainland China. Gregory also did a great deal for ties between China and the United States, including supporting education programs for Chinese students in both countries. His experiences and writings on China were the basis for a popular undergraduate course on the Chinese economy that Gregory taught regularly at Princeton for many years.
About Chow Institute Paula and Gregory Chow Institute for Studies in Economics is one of China’s leading centers for research, policy evaluation and academic training. First founded as Chow Center in 2016 under the auspice and generosity of Professor Gregory Chow, Chow Institute was upgraded to an independent institution in May 2022. Our founding Director is Professor Yongmiao Hong, who is the Ernest S. Liu Professor of Economics and International Studies Emeritus at Cornell University. Chow Institute is devoted to excellence in training academic candidates, producing original research, and facilitating dialogue of strong policy relevance.
Chow Institute embraces three research centers: the XMU-CAS Basic Science Center for Econometric Modelling and Economic Policy Studies (sponsored by the NSFC Basic Science Center Project), the MOE Key Laboratory of Econometrics (Xiamen University), and the XMU Center for Macroeconomic Research (an MOE Key Research Base in Social Sciences).
XMU-CAS Basic Science Center for Econometric Modelling and Economic Policy Studies is jointly managed by Chow Institute and the Center for Forecasting Science at Chinese Academy of Sciences. Approved in 2019, the Basic Science Center is the first national basic science center project not only in the Management Science Division of National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC), but also in Fujian Province and Xiamen University. Combining research strengths of Xiamen University and Chinese Academy of Sciences in the fields of econometrics, statistics and data science, forecasting science, policy studies, quantitative finance, international economics, environmental economics and climate change economics, the Basic Science Center actively promotes in-depth interdisciplinary exploration, and strives to deliver cutting-edge research. It is positioned to be an academic highland for econometric modeling and economic forecasting with international influence.
MOE Key Laboratory of Econometrics (Xiamen University) is among one of the first key laboratories of the Ministry of Education (MOE) founded in 2009. As China's first key laboratory in Economics, the Key Lab strives to promote econometrics education, research and international academic exchanges in Xiamen University and China.
XMU Center for Macroeconomic Research was established in September 2001 with a specific research agenda focusing on policy relevance. Since February 2005, the center has become a key research base in humanities and social sciences of the Ministry of Education. It is also one of the most important components of the National Philosophy and Social Science Innovation Base, and has long been engaging in China's macroeconomic analysis and forecasting research.
Mission and Goal Chow Institute is dedicated to becoming a leading economic institution that focuses on econometrics and quantitative policy analysis in China and Asia.
As an international hub for academic exchange, the institute is committed to rigorous theoretical work, innovative research paradigms, and interdisciplinary synergies. It also serves as a highly influential institute in policy research, providing evidence-based policy insights into areas such as economic growth, development, and social governance. Additionally, it is a premier center for training a group of academic talents with a strong theoretical foundation, who can apply cutting-edge econometrics methods and possess a deep understanding of China's econ
position.jp_keywords: econometrics, statistics and data science, economics, and finance.

position.jp_full_text:
Any field. Our preferred areas of specializations are – but not limited to – economic history, finance, health economics, international economics/trade, law and economics, macroeconomics, political economics, public economics, econometrics, statistics and data science.
Xiamen University (XMU) was established in 1921 by renowned overseas Chinese leader Mr. Tan Kah Kee, and is located in the resort-like island of Xiamen in Southeast China. Economics at XMU traces its origins to the Business Division at the founding of the university in 1921 with a long tradition of excellence in teaching and research. Under the leadership of Professor Wang Yanan, a former President of XMU and the Chinese translator of Karl Marx’s Das Kapital, the School of Economics (SOE) at Xiamen University has been one of the top programs in China since 1950s. As a strategic initiative to internationalize economics research and education, the Wang Yanan Institute for Studies in Economics (WISE) was established in 2005 with a strong focus on econometrics and other related fields.
The mission of WISE and the SOE is to nurture economic talents with cutting-edge quantitative skills and a global perspective that drive societal improvement, and our vision is to become a world-renowned leading Chinese education and research institution in economics. In QS World University Rankings by Subject 2025, we rank the 78th globally in Economics and Econometrics. In U.S. News Best Global University Rankings 2026-2027, we rank 22nd globally in Economics and Business.
Having successfully recruited more than 100 faculty members from abroad in the past few years, WISE and the SOE still have faculty positions available in all areas of economics, finance and statistics at all ranks.
Junior candidates are expected to have a Ph.D. degree by August 2027 and show evidence of promising research ability. Senior candidates must have a Ph.D. degree and a demonstrably strong research record. Competitive salary, research grant and housing subsidy are provided, with a regular teaching load of 2 courses per year. Additional course(s) may be arranged with commensurate pay. All faculty members, regardless of their citizenship, enjoy a housing subsidy for the first four years.
More information about us is available at the website https://wise.xmu.edu.cn/english/.
All applications will be reviewed and we will organize initial online interview for selected candidates.
Application via JOE portal or email are accepted. Please be noticed that all reference letters should be uploaded via JOE portal or sent directly from referrers to wiserecruit@xmu.edu.cn.
Applicants should also register and complete the online application via https://econpub.xmu.edu.cn/faculty/login.aspx
Contact Information: Recruiting Committee, c/o Ms. Daisy Youshu Xu, Wang Yanan Institute for Studies in Economics & School of Economics, Room N105, Economics Building, Xiamen University, Xiamen, 361005, Fujian, China or email wiserecruit@xmu.edu.cn.

The Yale School of the Environment (YSE) seeks applicants for an Assistant Professor position in Business & the Environment, Sustainable Finance, or Environmental Markets. We welcome scholars whose research connects business, finance, economics, marketing, supply chains, environmental markets, or related fields with environmental and natural resource challenges.
Research areas may include sustainable finance, environmental risk management, conservation and climate finance, commodity and environmental markets, consumer behavior, supply chains and logistics, land and resource markets, or environmental aspects of tax strategy. Candidates should demonstrate strong potential for impactful scholarship and interdisciplinary collaboration. The successful candidate will develop a nationally or internationally recognized research program, teach business-related courses to master’s and PhD students at YSE and The Forest School, and mentor graduate students.
Applicants must hold a PhD in finance, marketing, business, supply chain and logistics, economics, or a related interdisciplinary field with relevant doctoral-level training.
YSE offers a highly collaborative environment with strong connections to Yale’s School of Management, Yale Law School, and the Center for Business and Environment at Yale (CBEY), providing opportunities for interdisciplinary research and teaching.
Applications should include a CV, research statement, teaching statement, representative publication, and contact information for three references.

position.jp_full_text:
The Budget Lab, a policy research center at Yale Law School, is searching for one or more applied microeconomists.
The successful candidate will take a lead role in the analysis of current and proposed public policies. This entails developing research designs, policy questions, and work plans relevant to the Budget Lab’s work. In some cases, it requires building new modeling capacity for exploration of policy counterfactuals.
We are seeking candidates from a range of fields, with special (but not exclusive) interest in housing economics. Applicants should have experience with applied, policy-oriented quantitative research and an interest in communicating analytical results to policy audiences. The successful candidate will combine insights from economic theory and relevant institutional knowledge as they conduct empirical research and microsimulation analysis. Candidates should be comfortable working in a fast-paced, collaborative team that typically uses R.
The Budget Lab is a primarily remote-work organization. This role may be located in any of the states approved for remote work by Yale University pending approval.

position.jp_full_text:
The School of Economics at Zhejiang University (ZJU) invites applications for tenure-track positions at the Assistant Professor level or above, with an expected start date in 2027. Applicants should hold a Ph.D. in Economics or a related field by the time of appointment. We are especially interested in candidates whose research relates to Chinese Economy, AI + Economics, Finance, Macroeconomics, Microeconomics, Econometrics, Public Finance and Taxation, International Trade and Industrial Organization. Strong candidates from other fields are also welcomed to apply. Candidates with relevant work experience and a solid publication record are preferred.
The economics discipline at ZJU, inheriting the academic legacy of Qiushi Academy, was first established in 1929 as one of the earliest economics departments in China's institutions of higher education. After nearly a century of development, the School of Economics, ZJU has gradually evolved into a research-oriented and innovative institution with a solid academic foundation, distinctive strengths, and broad influence both domestically and internationally.
The School currently comprises 5 academic departments: the Department of Economics, the Department of Finance, the Department of International Economics and Trade, the Department of Labor Economics, and the Department of Public Finance. Focusing on national strategies for regional development, the School has built high-level platforms for academic research and think-tank services. It actively undertakes major national research projects and national high-end think-tank projects, and has developed strong academic reputation across fields including the private economy and socialist economic theory with Chinese characteristics, open economy and development, digital economy and macroeconomics, human capital and economic development, artificial intelligence and econometrics, macro-finance and digital finance, digital trade and green development, and digital public finance and government governance. It is ranked 21st for Economics and Business by U.S. News (2026) and 38th for Business and Economics by Times Higher Education (2026).
We offer a highly competitive and negotiable salary for faculty positions. Benefits may include start-up research fund (where applicable), housing subsidies (where applicable), housing accumulation fund, social insurance, etc.
Applicants should submit a cover letter, a curriculum vitae, a job market paper, representative research paper(s) and three signed reference letters by November 22, 2026.
All applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Shortlisted candidates will be notified for video interview. Only selected candidates will be notified.
For inquiries, please contact Ms. Gao at jjxy@zju.edu.cn.
position.jp_keywords: Chinese Economy AI + Economics Finance Macroeconomics Microeconomics Econometrics Public Finance and Taxation International Trade Industrial Organization
